bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第120卷 。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 120.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 120.

sentences.zh: 【宋紀二】起閼逢困敦，盡強圉單閼，凡四年。。

translations.literal: 【Song Records 2】 Beginning from Yanfeng Kundun through Qiangyu Shan'ge—in all, four years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Song Records 2】 From the year Yanfeng Kundun through Qiangyu Shan'ge—four years in all.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之上元嘉元年（甲子，公元四二四年） 。

translations.literal: Above, first part of the reign of Emperor Wen the Literary: Yuanjia year 1 (jiazi; 424 CE).
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 1, first year of the reign of Emperor Wen—above, part one (jiazi; 424 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，魏改元始光。。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Wei changed the era name to Shiguang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Northern Wei adopted the new reign title Shiguang.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，魏安定殤王彌卒。。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Prince Shang of Anding Mi of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day, Mi, Prince Shang of Anding in Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 營陽王居喪無禮，好與左右狎暱，遊戲無度。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yingyang observed mourning without propriety, was fond of intimacy with those at his side, and played without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yingyang failed to observe mourning decorum, delighted in familiar intimacy with his attendants, and indulged in unrestrained amusements.

sentences.zh: 特進致仕范泰上封事曰：「伏聞陛下時在後園，頗習武備，鼓鞞在宮，聲聞於外。

translations.literal: Fan Tai, specially advanced and retired, submitted a sealed memorial saying: "I have heard that Your Majesty is at times in the rear garden, practicing military preparations rather extensively; drums and war drums are within the palace, and the sound is heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tai, who held the rank of specially advanced and had retired from office, submitted a sealed memorial: "I have learned that Your Majesty often drills in military exercises in the rear garden; drums and martial music resound within the palace and can be heard beyond its walls.

sentences.zh: 黷武掖庭之內，喧嘩省闥之間，非徒不足以威四夷，只生遠近之怪。

translations.literal: To abuse military display within the inner palace and raise clamor between the gates of the Secretariat not only fails to awe the four barbarians but only gives rise to wonder near and far.
translations.idiomatic: To parade arms within the inner palace and raise a din at the gates of the Secretariat will not overawe the four quarters; it can only breed astonishment near and far.

sentences.zh: 陛下踐祚，委政宰臣，實用高宗諒暗之美；

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, you entrusted government to the chief ministers, truly applying the fine example of Gaozong's mourning seclusion;
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first took the throne, you entrusted affairs to your chief ministers, in the fine spirit of Gaozong's mourning seclusion;

sentences.zh: 而更親狎小人，懼非社稷至計，經世之道也。」

translations.literal: yet now you draw close to petty men instead—I fear this is not the supreme plan for the altars of state, nor the way to order the age."
translations.idiomatic: yet now you draw close to petty men instead—I fear this is no sound policy for the altars of state, nor a way to govern the age."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 泰，寧之子也。。

translations.literal: Tai was the son of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tai was a son of Fan Ning.

sentences.zh: 南豫州刺史廬陵王義真，警悟愛文義，而性輕易，與太子左衛率謝靈運、員外常侍顏延之、慧琳道人情好款密。

translations.literal: Liu Yizhen, Prince of Luling and governor of South Yuzhou, was quick-witted and loved literary learning, but his nature was frivolous; he was on terms of warm intimacy with Xie Lingyun, left guard leader of the crown prince, Yan Yanzhi, attendant at large, and the monk Huilin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhen, Prince of Luling and governor of South Yuzhou, was bright and fond of letters, but light and unserious in character; he kept close, affectionate company with Xie Lingyun, commander of the crown prince's left guard, Yan Yanzhi, attendant at large, and the monk Huilin.

sentences.zh: 嘗云：「得志之日，以靈運、延之為宰相，慧琳為西豫州都督。」

translations.literal: He once said: "When I attain my aim, I shall make Lingyun and Yanzhi chief ministers, and Huilin military governor of West Yuzhou."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "When my day comes, I shall make Lingyun and Yanzhi chief ministers, and Huilin military governor of West Yuzhou."

sentences.zh: 靈運，玄之孫也，性褊傲，不遵法度，朝廷但以文義處之，不以為有實用。

translations.literal: Lingyun was a grandson of Xie Xuan; by nature narrow and arrogant, he did not observe law and regulation; the court treated him only for his literary accomplishments and did not regard him as of practical use.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun was a grandson of Xie Xuan—proud, impatient, and heedless of rules. The court valued him only for his literary gifts and did not count him fit for practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 靈運自謂才能宜參權要，常懷憤邑。

translations.literal: Lingyun considered his talent fit to share in power at the center and constantly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun believed his talents entitled him to a share in high power and nursed a constant grievance.

sentences.zh: 延之，含之曾孫也，嗜酒放縱。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was a great-grandson of Yan Han and was addicted to wine and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi was a great-grandson of Yan Han and was given to drink and dissolute conduct.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之等惡義真與靈運等游，義真故吏范晏從容戒之，義真曰：「靈運空疏，延之隘薄，魏文帝所謂『古今文人類不護細行』者也；

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi and the others disliked Yizhen's association with Lingyun and the rest. Fan Yan, a former subordinate of Yizhen, gently admonished him. Yizhen said: "Lingyun is empty and shallow, Yanzhi narrow and mean—men of the sort of whom Emperor Wen of Wei said, 'Writers of past and present alike are careless of small conduct';
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi and his colleagues resented Yizhen's intimacy with Lingyun and the others. Fan Yan, a former officer under Yizhen, cautioned him gently. Yizhen replied, "Lingyun is shallow and ungrounded, Yanzhi petty and mean—just the sort Emperor Wen of Wei had in mind when he said that writers ancient and modern alike are careless of small conduct;

sentences.zh: 但性情所得，未能忘言於悟賞耳。」

translations.literal: yet in what our temperaments share we cannot but speak freely in mutual appreciation."
translations.idiomatic: yet in what our temperaments share, we cannot help speaking freely in mutual delight."

sentences.zh: 於是羨之等以為運、延之構扇異同，非毀執政，出靈運為永嘉太守，延之為始安太守。。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xianzhi and the others judged that Lingyun and Yanzhi were stirring up factions and slandering those in power; Lingyun was sent out as administrator of Yongjia and Yanzhi as administrator of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xianzhi and his colleagues decided that Lingyun and Yanzhi were stirring faction and slandering the government; Lingyun was posted as administrator of Yongjia and Yanzhi as administrator of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 義真至歷陽，多所求索，執政每裁量不盡與。

translations.literal: When Yizhen reached Liyang he made many demands; the ministers in power each time measured and did not grant all he asked.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhen reached Liyang he made many demands, and those in power each time weighed his requests and refused to grant all he wanted.

sentences.zh: 義真深怨之，數有不平之言，又表求還都。

translations.literal: Yizhen deeply resented this, repeatedly uttered words of grievance, and also memorialized asking to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen nursed a deep resentment, spoke repeatedly of injustice, and also submitted a memorial asking to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 咨議參軍廬江何尚之屢諫，不聽。

translations.literal: He Shangzhi of Lujiang, advisory staff officer, remonstrated repeatedly; he was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He Shangzhi of Lujiang, a staff adviser, remonstrated again and again, but Yizhen would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時羨之等已密謀廢帝，而次立者應在義眞；

translations.literal: At this time Xianzhi and the others had already secretly plotted to depose the emperor, and the one next in line to succeed ought to have been Yizhen;
translations.idiomatic: By then Xianzhi and his colleagues had already plotted in secret to depose the emperor, and the man next in line for the throne should have been Yizhen;

sentences.zh: 乃因義眞與帝有隙，先奏列其罪惡，廢為庶人，徙新安郡。

translations.literal: therefore, because Yizhen and the emperor were at odds, they first memorialized listing his crimes, deposed him to commoner status, and banished him to Xin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: so, using the rift between Yizhen and the emperor, they first memorialized listing his offenses, stripped him of rank to commoner status, and banished him to Xin'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 前吉陽令堂邑張約之上疏曰：「廬陵王少蒙先皇優慈之遇，長受陛下睦受之恩，故在心必言，所懷必亮，容犯臣子之道，致招驕瓷之愆。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuezhi of Tangyi, former magistrate of Jiyang, submitted a memorial saying: "The Prince of Luling in youth received the late emperor's gracious favor, and in maturity has enjoyed Your Majesty's cordial kindness; therefore what is in his heart he must speak, what he feels he must make clear—he may have transgressed the way of subject and son and thereby incurred the fault of arrogant insolence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuezhi of Tangyi, former magistrate of Jiyang, submitted a memorial: "The Prince of Luling in youth enjoyed the late emperor's gracious favor, and as a man has received Your Majesty's warm kindness; therefore what is in his heart he must speak, and what he feels he must make plain. He may have overstepped a subject's duty and drawn the charge of arrogant insolence.

sentences.zh: 至於天恣夙成，實有卓然之美，宜在容養，靈善掩瑕，訓盡議方，進退以漸。

translations.literal: As to his heaven-endowed gifts matured from of old, he truly has outstanding excellence; he ought to be nurtured with forbearance, his good points cherished and his flaws covered, instructed fully and counseled by every means, advanced and withdrawn by gradual steps.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his natural gifts have long been formed, and he truly has outstanding qualities. He ought to be nurtured with patience, his virtues cherished and his flaws overlooked, instructed fully and guided by every proper means, advanced or restrained by gradual steps.

sentences.zh: 今猥加剝辱，幽徙遠郡，上傷陛下常棣之篤，下令遠近恇然失圖。

translations.literal: Now to heap on him stripping and disgrace and banish him in seclusion to a distant commandery wounds above Your Majesty's deep fraternal bond and below leaves near and far alarmed and without a plan.
translations.idiomatic: To heap disgrace upon him now and banish him in seclusion to a distant commandery wounds Your Majesty's deep brotherly bond above and leaves men near and far alarmed and without counsel below.

sentences.zh: 臣伏思大宋開基造次，根條未繁，宜廣樹籓戚，敦睦以道。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that the Great Song, in the haste of founding its foundation, has roots and branches not yet abundant; it is fitting to plant broadly among the imperial kin and cultivate harmony by the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant reflects that the Song, in the haste of founding, has not yet put down deep roots; it is fitting to extend the imperial kindred broadly and bind them in harmony by right principle.

sentences.zh: 人誰無過，貴能自新；

translations.literal: Who among men is without fault? What matters is the ability to renew oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Who among men is without fault? What matters is the power to reform;

sentences.zh: 以武皇之愛子，陛下之懿弟，豈可以其一眚，長致淪棄哉！」

translations.literal: as a son beloved of Emperor Wu and Your Majesty's worthy younger brother—how can one fault forever cast him down to ruin!"
translations.idiomatic: as a son beloved of Emperor Wu and Your Majesty's worthy younger brother—how can a single fault condemn him to lasting ruin!"

sentences.zh: 書奏，以約之為梁州府參軍，尋殺之。。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Yuezhi was made a staff officer of the Liangzhou headquarters, and soon afterward was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was received, Yuezhi was appointed a staff officer in the Liangzhou headquarters—and soon afterward was put to death.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲辰，魏主東巡大寧。。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen, the Wei ruler toured east to Daning.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on jiachen day, the Wei emperor made an eastern tour to Daning.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐遣鎮南將軍吉毘等帥步騎一萬，南伐白苟、車孚、崔提、旁為四國，皆降之。。

translations.literal: Qifu Chipan, King of Qin, sent the southern-pacifying general Ji Pi and others to lead ten thousand foot and horse south to attack the four states of Baigou, Chefu, Cuiti, and Pangwei; all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan, King of Qin, sent the southern-pacifying general Ji Pi and others at the head of ten thousand infantry and cavalry on a southern campaign against the four states of Baigou, Chefu, Cuiti, and Pangwei; all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之等以南兗州刺史檀道濟先朝舊將，威服殿省，且有兵眾，乃召道濟及江州刺史王弘入朝；

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi and the others, because Tan Daoji, governor of South Yanzhou, was an old general of the previous reign, awe-inspiring in the palace offices and possessed of troops, summoned Daoji and Wang Hong, governor of Jiangzhou, to court;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi and his colleagues, because Tan Daoji of South Yanzhou was a veteran general of the previous reign who commanded respect in the palace offices and held troops, summoned Daoji and Wang Hong, governor of Jiangzhou, to court;

sentences.zh: 五月，皆至建康，廢立之謀告之。。

translations.literal: in the fifth month both reached Jiankang, and the plot to depose and enthrone was disclosed to them.
translations.idiomatic: in the fifth month both reached Jiankang, and the plot to depose the emperor and enthrone another was revealed to them.

sentences.zh: 甲申，謝晦以領軍府屋敗，悉令家人出外，聚將士於府內；

translations.literal: On jiashen, Xie Hui, because the headquarters of the directorate of the guards had dilapidated buildings, ordered all his household outside and gathered officers and soldiers within the compound;
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day, Xie Hui, finding the headquarters of the directorate of the guards in disrepair, sent all his household outside and assembled officers and soldiers within the compound;

sentences.zh: 又使中書舍人邢安泰、潘盛為內應。

translations.literal: and also had the secretaries Xing Antai and Pan Sheng act as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: he also stationed the secretaries Xing Antai and Pan Sheng inside as collaborators.

sentences.zh: 夜，邀檀道濟同宿，晦悚動不得眠，道濟就寢便熟，晦以此服之。。

translations.literal: At night he invited Tan Daoji to lodge with him; Hui was agitated and could not sleep, but Daoji lay down and at once slept soundly—Hui thereby came to admire him.
translations.idiomatic: That night he invited Tan Daoji to lodge with him. Hui was restless and could not sleep, but Daoji lay down and slept soundly at once—whereupon Hui came to respect him.

sentences.zh: 時帝於華林園為列肆，親自沽賣，以與左右引船為樂，夕，游天淵池，即龍舟而寢。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor had set up rows of shops in the Hualin Garden, personally buying and selling, taking pleasure with those at his side in drawing boats; in the evening he roamed the Tianyuan Pool and slept at once on the dragon boat.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor had set up rows of market stalls in the Hualin Garden and sold goods himself, amusing himself with his attendants by towing boats; in the evening he roamed the Tianyuan Pool and went straight to sleep on the imperial dragon boat.

sentences.zh: 乙酉詰旦，道濟引兵居前，羨之等繼其後，入自雲龍門；

translations.literal: At dawn on yiyou, Daoji led troops in the van and Xianzhi and the others followed, entering by the Yunlong Gate;
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on yiyou day, Daoji led troops in the van while Xianzhi and the others followed, entering through the Yunlong Gate;

sentences.zh: 安泰等先誡宿衛，莫有御者。

translations.literal: Antai and the others had beforehand warned the night guards, and none resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Antai and the others had already warned the night guards, and none offered resistance.

sentences.zh: 帝未興，軍士進殺二侍者，傷帝指，扶出東閣，收璽綬，群臣拜辭，衛送故太子宮。。

translations.literal: The emperor had not yet risen; soldiers advanced and killed two attendants, wounded the emperor's finger, supported him out to the eastern pavilion, took the seals and cords, the officials bowed in farewell, and guards escorted him to the former crown prince's palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not yet risen. Soldiers rushed in, killed two attendants, wounded the emperor's finger, helped him out to the eastern pavilion, took the seals and cords of office, the officials bowed in farewell, and guards escorted him to the former crown prince's palace.

sentences.zh: 侍中程道惠勸羨之等立皇弟南豫州刺史義恭。

translations.literal: Cheng Daohui, palace attendant, urged Xianzhi and the others to enthrone the emperor's younger brother Yigong, governor of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Daohui, palace attendant, urged Xianzhi and his colleagues to enthrone the emperor's younger brother Yigong, governor of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 羨之等以宜都王義隆素有令望，又多符瑞，乃稱皇太后令，數帝過惡，廢為營陽王，以宜都王辰承大統，赦死罪以下。

translations.literal: Xianzhi and the others, because Prince Yilong of Yidu had long enjoyed fine repute and there were many portents, then proclaimed an order of the empress dowager listing the emperor's faults, deposed him as Prince of Yingyang, and on the day chen installed the Prince of Yidu to receive the great succession, granting amnesty below the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi and his colleagues, because Prince Yilong of Yidu had long enjoyed a fine reputation and many auspicious signs had appeared, proclaimed an order of the empress dowager listing the emperor's offenses, deposed him as Prince of Yingyang, and on chen day installed the Prince of Yidu as heir to the throne, granting amnesty for all crimes short of death.

sentences.zh: 又稱皇大後令，奉還璽綬；

translations.literal: They also proclaimed an order of the grand empress dowager returning the seals and cords;
translations.idiomatic: They also proclaimed an order of the grand empress dowager returning the seals and cords of office;

sentences.zh: 並廢皇后為營陽王妃，遷營陽王於吳。

translations.literal: and at the same time deposed the empress to Princess of Yingyang and moved the Prince of Yingyang to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: and at the same time reduced the empress to Princess of Yingyang and moved the Prince of Yingyang to Wu.

sentences.zh: 使檀道濟入守朝堂。

translations.literal: They sent Tan Daoji in to guard the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Tan Daoji in to hold the court hall.

sentences.zh: 王至吳，止金昌亭；

translations.literal: When the prince reached Wu he stopped at Jinchang Pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: When the prince reached Wu he lodged at Jinchang Pavilion;

sentences.zh: 六月，癸丑，羨之等使邢安泰就弒之。

translations.literal: in the sixth month, on guichou, Xianzhi and the others sent Xing Antai to go and assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth month, on guichou day, Xianzhi and his colleagues sent Xing Antai to assassinate him.

sentences.zh: 王多力，突走出昌門，追者以門關踣而弒之。。

translations.literal: The prince was very strong; he burst out through Chang Gate, and the pursuers, using the gate bar, tripped and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was very strong; he broke out through Chang Gate, and his pursuers struck him down with the gate bar and killed him.

sentences.zh: 裴子野論曰：古者人君養子，能言而師授之辭，能行而傅相之禮。

translations.literal: Pei Ziye remarked: In antiquity when a ruler reared a son, once he could speak a teacher was appointed to instruct him in speech, and once he could walk a tutor and aide were appointed with the proper rites.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye remarked: In antiquity, when a ruler reared a son, once the child could speak a teacher was appointed to instruct him in speech; once he could walk, tutor and aide were appointed with the proper rites.

sentences.zh: 宋之教誨，雅異於斯，居中則任僕妾，處外則近趨走。

translations.literal: Song instruction differed markedly from this: within the palace they relied on servant-girls and concubines; outside they kept close to runners and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Song practice in rearing heirs differed sharply from this: within the palace they relied on servant-girls and concubines; outside they kept runners and attendants close at hand.

sentences.zh: 太子、皇子，有帥，有侍，是二職者，皆台皁也。

translations.literal: For crown princes and imperial sons there were commanders and attendants—these two offices were all men of low station.
translations.idiomatic: Crown princes and imperial sons had commanders and attendants—and both offices were filled by men of low rank.

sentences.zh: 制其行止，授其法則，導達臧否，罔弗由之；

translations.literal: They controlled their comings and goings, handed down rules and models, guided and conveyed approval and blame—nothing was not done through them;
translations.idiomatic: They controlled their movements, handed down rules and models, guided and conveyed praise and blame—nothing was done except through them;

sentences.zh: 言不及於禮義，識不達於今古，謹敕者能勸之以吝嗇，狂愚者或誘之以凶慝。

translations.literal: speech did not reach to ritual and righteousness, understanding did not penetrate present and past; the cautious and obedient could be urged toward stinginess, the wild and foolish sometimes enticed toward wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: their speech never rose to ritual and righteousness, their understanding never reached present and past; the cautious might be urged toward miserliness, the reckless sometimes lured toward wickedness.

sentences.zh: 雖有師傅，多以耆艾大夫為之；

translations.literal: Although there were masters and tutors, for the most part venerable grandees filled these posts;
translations.idiomatic: Though there were masters and tutors, for the most part aged grandees filled those posts;

sentences.zh: 雖有友及文學，多以膏粱年少為之；

translations.literal: although there were companions and literary scholars, for the most part pampered young men of good family filled these posts;
translations.idiomatic: though there were companions and literary scholars, for the most part pampered young men of good family filled those posts;

sentences.zh: 具位而已，亦弗與游。

translations.literal: they held title only and were not admitted to association.
translations.idiomatic: they held title only and were not admitted to real companionship.

sentences.zh: 幼王臨州，長史行事；

translations.literal: When a young prince governed a province, the chief administrator conducted affairs;
translations.idiomatic: When a young prince governed a province, the chief administrator conducted affairs;

sentences.zh: 宣傳教命，又有典簽；

translations.literal: to proclaim and transmit orders there was also the registry clerk;
translations.idiomatic: to proclaim and transmit orders there was also the registry clerk;

sentences.zh: 往往專恣，竊弄威權，是以本枝雖茂而端良甚寡。

translations.literal: who often acted with arbitrary license and secretly wielded authority—thus though the root and branches were abundant, upright and worthy men were very few.
translations.idiomatic: who often acted with arbitrary license and secretly wielded authority—so that though the imperial house was numerous, upright and worthy princes were very few.

sentences.zh: 嗣君沖幼，世繼奸回，雖惡物丑類，天然自出，然習則生常，其流遠矣。

translations.literal: Succession rulers were young and tender, generation after generation inherited treacherous and perverse ways; though vile things and ugly types are born of nature, habit becomes second nature and the current runs far.
translations.idiomatic: Succession rulers were young and tender, and generation after generation inherited treacherous ways; though wickedness springs from nature, habit becomes second nature, and the current runs deep.

sentences.zh: 降及太宗，舉天下而棄之，亦暱比之為也。

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Taizong, who cast away all under Heaven—it too was the work of such intimate associations.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Emperor Taizong, who cast away all under Heaven—it too was the fruit of such intimate associations.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 有國有家，其鑒之矣！。

translations.literal: Those who possess a state and a clan—let them take this as a mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Let those who hold a state and a clan take this as their mirror!

sentences.zh: 傅亮帥行台百官奉法駕迎宜都王於江陵。」

translations.literal: Fu Liang led the officials of the traveling secretariat with the imperial equipage to welcome the Prince of Yidu at Jiangling."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang led the officials of the traveling secretariat with the imperial equipage to welcome the Prince of Yidu at Jiangling."

sentences.zh: 祠部尚書蔡廓至尋陽，遇疾不堪前；

translations.literal: Cai Kuo, minister of the directorate of sacrifices, reached Xunyang but fell ill and could not go on;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Kuo, minister of the directorate of sacrifices, reached Xunyang but fell ill and could not continue;

sentences.zh: 亮與之別。

translations.literal: Liang took leave of him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang took leave of him.

sentences.zh: 廓曰：「營陽在吳，宜厚加供奉；

translations.literal: Kuo said: "The Prince of Yingyang is in Wu; he ought to be generously supplied;
translations.idiomatic: Kuo said, "The Prince of Yingyang is in Wu; he ought to be generously provided for;

sentences.zh: 一旦不幸，卿諸人有弒主之名，欲立於世，將可得邪！」

translations.literal: if misfortune should come upon him one day, you gentlemen will bear the name of regicide—do you think you could still stand in the world!"
translations.idiomatic: if misfortune should befall him, you gentlemen will bear the name of regicide—do you imagine you could still stand in the world!"

sentences.zh: 時亮已與羨之議害營陽王，乃馳信止之，不及。

translations.literal: At this time Liang had already discussed with Xianzhi harming the Prince of Yingyang; he therefore sent a fast message to stop it, but did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: By then Liang had already agreed with Xianzhi to kill the Prince of Yingyang; he sent an urgent message to stop it, but arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 羨之大怒曰：「與人共計議，如何旋背即賣惡於人邪？」

translations.literal: Xianzhi was greatly angered and said: "When one plots together with others, how can one turn at once and sell the evil to others?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi flew into a rage: "When men plot together, how can you turn at once and cast the blame on others?"

sentences.zh: 羨之等以遣使者殺前廬陵王義真於新安。。

translations.literal: Xianzhi and the others thereupon sent envoys to kill the former Prince of Luling Yizhen at Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi and his colleagues then sent envoys to kill the former Prince of Luling, Yizhen, at Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 羨之以荊州地重，恐宜都王至，或別用人，乃亟以錄命除領軍將軍謝晦行都督荊、湘等七州諸軍事、荊州刺史，欲令居外為援，精兵舊將，悉以配之。。

translations.literal: Xianzhi, because Jingzhou's territory was weighty and he feared that when the Prince of Yidu arrived someone else might be appointed, urgently issued a recorded order appointing the director-general of the guards Xie Hui acting commander of all military affairs in Jing, Xiang, and seven other provinces and governor of Jingzhou, intending to have him stay outside as support; picked troops and old generals were all assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi, because Jingzhou was strategically vital and he feared that when the Prince of Yidu arrived another man might be placed there, urgently issued a recorded order appointing Xie Hui, director-general of the guards, acting commander of military affairs in Jing, Xiang, and seven other provinces and governor of Jingzhou, intending to keep him outside as a support; elite troops and veteran generals were all assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，行台至江陵，立行門於城南，題曰「大司馬門」。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the traveling secretariat reached Jiangling, set up a traveling gate south of the city, and inscribed it "Gate of the Grand Marshal."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, the traveling secretariat reached Jiangling, erected a traveling gate south of the city, and inscribed it "Gate of the Grand Marshal."

sentences.zh: 傅亮帥百僚詣門上表，進璽紱，儀物甚盛，宜都王時年十八，下教曰：「猥以不德，廖降大命，顧己兢悸，何以克堪！

translations.literal: Fu Liang led the hundred officials to the gate to submit a memorial, presenting the seals and cords; the ceremonial objects were very grand. The Prince of Yidu was then eighteen years old. He issued an order saying: "I am unworthy to have been so undeservedly granted the great mandate; looking upon myself I am fearful and trembling—how could I bear it!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang led the hundred officials to the gate to submit a memorial presenting the seals and cords; the ceremonial display was magnificent. The Prince of Yidu was then eighteen. He issued an order: "Unworthy as I am, I have been undeservedly granted the great mandate; looking upon myself I tremble with fear—how could I bear it!

sentences.zh: 輒當暫歸朝廷，展哀陵寢，並與賢彥申寫所懷。

translations.literal: I shall for the present return to the court, display mourning at the imperial tombs, and together with worthy ministers set forth what is in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I shall for the present return to court, pay mourning at the imperial tombs, and together with worthy ministers set forth what is in my heart.

sentences.zh: 望體其心，勿為辭費。

translations.literal: I hope you will enter into my intent and not make a fuss of declining.
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will understand my intent and spare me elaborate refusals.

sentences.zh: 府州佐史並稱臣，請題榜諸門，一依宮省；

translations.literal: The staff officers of the prefecture and province all styled themselves subjects and asked to inscribe plaques on the various gates, all according to the palace offices;
translations.idiomatic: The staff officers of the prefecture and province all styled themselves subjects and asked to inscribe plaques on the gates after the palace model;

sentences.zh: 王皆不許。

translations.literal: the prince would not permit any of it.
translations.idiomatic: the prince refused every request.

sentences.zh: 教州、府、國綱紀宥所統內見刑，原逋責。。

translations.literal: He ordered that within the jurisdictions of the province, prefecture, and principality, discipline should pardon those under sentence within the governed areas and remit overdue levies.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that within the province, prefecture, and principality those under sentence in his jurisdiction be pardoned and overdue levies remitted.

sentences.zh: 諸將佐聞營陽、廬陵王死，皆以為疑，勸王不可東下。

translations.literal: When the generals and staff officers heard that the Princes of Yingyang and Luling were dead, all were suspicious and urged the prince not to go east.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals and staff officers learned that the Princes of Yingyang and Luling were dead, all were suspicious and urged the prince not to go east.

sentences.zh: 司馬王華曰：「先帝有大功於天下，四海所服；

translations.literal: Wang Hua, chief administrator, said: "The late emperor had great merit for all under Heaven and was obeyed by the four seas;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua, chief administrator, said, "The late emperor rendered great service to the realm and was obeyed throughout the four seas;

sentences.zh: 雖嗣主不綱，人望未改。

translations.literal: Although the succession ruler did not hold the reins, the people's regard had not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Though the succession ruler had lost his way, popular esteem for the house had not changed.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之中才寒士，傅亮布衣諸生，非有晉宣帝、王大將軍之心明矣；

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi is a man of middling talent and humble birth, Fu Liang a commoner and mere student—clearly they do not have the hearts of Emperor Xuan of Jin or the Great General Wang;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi is a man of middling talent from humble stock, Fu Liang a commoner and mere scholar—clearly they lack the ambition of Emperor Xuan of Jin or Grand General Wang;

sentences.zh: 受寄崇重，未容遽敢背德。

translations.literal: entrusted with weighty charge, they could not lightly dare to turn against virtue.
translations.idiomatic: entrusted with a weighty charge, they could hardly dare to turn against their trust at once.

sentences.zh: 畏廬陵嚴斷，將來必不自容；

translations.literal: They feared the Prince of Luling's stern decisiveness and that in the future they could not contain themselves;
translations.idiomatic: They feared the Prince of Luling's stern decisiveness and knew they could not survive his rule;

sentences.zh: 以殿下寬睿慈仁，遠近所知，且越次奉迎，冀以見德；

translations.literal: because Your Highness is known near and far for generous wisdom and humane kindness, and because they welcomed you out of turn, hoping thereby to show virtue;
translations.idiomatic: because Your Highness is known near and far for generous wisdom and humane kindness, and because they welcomed you out of turn, hoping thereby to show their virtue;

sentences.zh: 悠悠之論，殆必不然。

translations.literal: the loose talk of the multitude is probably not so.
translations.idiomatic: the loose talk abroad is almost certainly wrong.

sentences.zh: 又，羨之等五人，同功並位，孰肯相讓！

translations.literal: Moreover, Xianzhi and the other five shared merit and rank equally—who would yield to whom!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Xianzhi and the other five shared merit and rank equally—who among them would yield to another!

sentences.zh: 就懷不軌，勢必不行。

translations.literal: Even if they harbored disloyal intent, the situation would necessarily not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they harbored treasonous intent, the situation would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 廢主若存，慮其將來受禍，致此殺害；

translations.literal: If the deposed ruler had lived, they feared he would suffer harm in the future and therefore brought about these killings;
translations.idiomatic: If the deposed ruler had lived, they feared future retribution and therefore brought about these killings;

sentences.zh: 蓋由貪生過深，寧敢一朝頓懷逆志！

translations.literal: it was because their greed for life ran too deep—they would hardly dare in a single morning to harbor rebellious intent!
translations.idiomatic: it sprang from an excessive fear for their lives—they would hardly dare in a single morning to harbor rebellious intent!

sentences.zh: 不過欲握權自固，以少主仰待耳。

translations.literal: they only wished to grasp power to secure themselves, relying on a young ruler to look up to them.
translations.idiomatic: They only wished to hold power and secure themselves, counting on a young ruler to depend on them.

sentences.zh: 殿下但當長驅六轡，以副天人之心。」

translations.literal: Your Highness need only drive the six reins straight on to answer the hearts of Heaven and men."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness need only drive straight on to answer the hearts of Heaven and men."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「卿復欲為宋昌邪！」

translations.literal: The prince said: "Do you wish to play Song Chang again!"
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "Are you trying to play Song Chang again!"

sentences.zh: 長史王曇首、南蠻校尉到彥之皆勸王行，曇首仍陳天人符應。

translations.literal: The chief administrator Wang Tanshou and the southern barbarian commandant Dao Yanzi both urged the prince to go; Tanshou also set forth heavenly and human portents.
translations.idiomatic: The chief administrator Wang Tanshou and the southern barbarian commandant Dao Yanzi both urged the prince to go east; Tanshou also cited heavenly and human portents.

sentences.zh: 王乃曰：』諸公受遺，不容背義。

translations.literal: The prince then said: "The lords received the late emperor's charge and cannot be allowed to betray righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then said, "These men received the late emperor's charge; they cannot be allowed to betray their trust.

sentences.zh: 且勞臣舊將，內外充滿，今兵力又足以制物，夫何所疑！」

translations.literal: Moreover, meritorious ministers and old generals fill court and camp inside and out; now our forces are also sufficient to control affairs—what is there to doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, meritorious ministers and veteran generals fill court and camp; our forces are sufficient to control affairs—what is there to doubt!"

sentences.zh: 乃命王華總後任，留鎮荊州。

translations.literal: He then ordered Wang Hua to take overall charge of rear affairs and remain to guard Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Wang Hua to take charge of rear affairs and remain to guard Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王欲使到彥之將兵前驅，彥之曰：「了彼不反，便應朝服順流；

translations.literal: The prince wished to have Dao Yanzi lead troops as vanguard. Yanzi said: "If we know they will not rebel, we ought to go in court dress down the current;
translations.idiomatic: The prince wished to have Dao Yanzi lead troops as vanguard. Yanzi said, "If we know they will not rebel, we ought to go in court dress downriver;

sentences.zh: 若使有虞，此師既不足恃，更開嫌隙之端，非所以副遠邇之望也。」

translations.literal: if there should be cause for concern, this force would not be enough to rely on and would only open a breach of suspicion—not the way to answer the hopes of near and far."
translations.idiomatic: if there should be trouble, this force would not suffice and would only open a breach of suspicion—not the way to answer the hopes of near and far."

sentences.zh: 會雍州刺史褚叔度卒，乃遣彥之權鎮襄陽。。

translations.literal: It happened that Chu Shudu, governor of Yongzhou, died; he therefore sent Yanzi provisionally to hold Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Chu Shudu, governor of Yongzhou, died; he therefore sent Yanzi provisionally to hold Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，王發江陵，引見傅亮，號泣，哀動左右。

translations.literal: On jiaxu the prince set out from Jiangling, summoned Fu Liang for audience, and wailed; his grief moved those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day the prince set out from Jiangling, summoned Fu Liang for audience, and wept aloud; his grief moved all who were near.

sentences.zh: 既而問義真及少帝薨廢本末，悲哭嗚咽，侍側都莫能仰視。

translations.literal: He then asked the full story of Yizhen's death and the young emperor's deposition and demise, weeping and sobbing; none of those attending at his side dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked the full story of Yizhen's death and the young emperor's deposition and demise, weeping and sobbing; none of those attending dared look up.

sentences.zh: 亮流汗沾背，不能對；

translations.literal: Liang sweated until his back was soaked and could not reply;
translations.idiomatic: Liang sweated until his back was soaked and could not reply;

sentences.zh: 乃布腹心於到彥之、王華等，深自結納。

translations.literal: he then opened his inmost heart to Dao Yanzi, Wang Hua, and the rest and bound himself to them deeply.
translations.idiomatic: he then confided his inmost thoughts to Dao Yanzi, Wang Hua, and the rest and bound himself to them deeply.

sentences.zh: 王以府州文武嚴兵自衛，台所遣百官眾力不得近部伍。

translations.literal: The prince had the civil and military officers of the prefecture and province guard him with strict troops; the hundred officials sent by the central government could not bring their forces near his ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had the civil and military officers of the prefecture and province guard him with strict troops; the hundred officials sent from the capital could not bring their forces near his ranks.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍朱容子抱刀處王所乘舟戶外，不解帶者累旬。

translations.literal: Zhu Rongzi, staff officer of the central guard, held his blade at the door of the boat the prince rode and did not ungird his sword for many tens of days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Rongzi, staff officer of the central guard, held his blade at the door of the prince's boat and did not ungird his sword for many tens of days.

sentences.zh: 魏主還宮。。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐遣太子暮末帥征北將軍木弈乾等步騎三萬，出貂渠谷，攻河西白草嶺、臨松郡，皆破之，徙民二萬餘口而還。。

translations.literal: Qifu Chipan, King of Qin, sent the crown prince Mumo at the head of the northern-campaigning general Muyigan and others with thirty thousand foot and horse out through Diaochu Valley to attack Baicao Ridge and Lin song commandery in Hexi; all were defeated, and more than twenty thousand households were moved before they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan, King of Qin, sent the crown prince Mumo at the head of the northern-campaigning general Muyigan and others with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry through Diaochu Valley to attack Baicao Ridge and Linsong commandery in Hexi; all were defeated, and more than twenty thousand households were relocated before they returned.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙申，宜都王至建康，群臣迎拜於新亭。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingshen, the Prince of Yidu reached Jiankang; the officials welcomed and bowed at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingshen day, the Prince of Yidu reached Jiankang; the officials welcomed and bowed at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之問傅亮曰：「王可方誰？」

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi asked Fu Liang: "To whom may the prince be compared?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi asked Fu Liang, "To whom may the prince be compared?"

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「晉文、景以上人。」

translations.literal: Liang said: "A man above Emperor Wen and Emperor Jing of Jin."
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "A man above Emperor Wen and Emperor Jing of Jin."

sentences.zh: 羨之曰：「必能明我赤心。」

translations.literal: Xianzhi said: "He will surely make clear my loyal heart."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi said, "He will surely understand my loyal heart."

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「不然。」。

translations.literal: Liang said: "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "Not so."

sentences.zh: 丁酉，王謁初寧陵，還，止中堂。

translations.literal: On dingyou the prince visited Chuning Mausoleum, returned, and stopped at the central hall.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day the prince visited Chuning Mausoleum, returned, and stopped at the central hall.

sentences.zh: 百官奉璽綬，王辭讓數四，乃受之，即皇帝位於中堂。

translations.literal: The hundred officials presented the seals and cords; the prince declined several times and then accepted, taking the imperial throne at the central hall.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials presented the seals and cords; the prince declined several times, then accepted and took the imperial throne at the central hall.

sentences.zh: 備法駕入宮，御太極前殿，大赦，改元，文武賜位二等。。

translations.literal: With full imperial equipage he entered the palace, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name, and granted the civil and military ranks two steps.
translations.idiomatic: With full imperial equipage he entered the palace, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name, and raised civil and military ranks by two steps.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，謁太廟。

translations.literal: On wuxu he visited the imperial ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day he visited the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 詔復廬陵王先封，迎其柩及孫修華、謝妃還建康。。

translations.literal: An edict restored the Prince of Luling's former fief and brought back his coffin together with Sun Xiuhua and Consort Xie to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored the Prince of Luling's former fief and brought back his coffin, together with Sun Xiuhua and Consort Xie, to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以行荊州刺史謝晦為真。

translations.literal: On gengzi the acting governor of Jingzhou Xie Hui was confirmed in office.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day the acting governor of Jingzhou, Xie Hui, was confirmed in office.

sentences.zh: 晦將行，與蔡廓別，屏人問曰：「吾其免乎？」

translations.literal: As Hui was about to depart he took leave of Cai Kuo, dismissed others, and asked: "Will I escape harm?"
translations.idiomatic: As Hui was about to depart he took leave of Cai Kuo, dismissed others, and asked, "Will I escape harm?"

sentences.zh: 廓曰：「卿受先帝顧命，任以社稷，廢昏立明，義無不可。

translations.literal: Kuo said: "You received the late emperor's dying charge and were entrusted with the altars of state; to depose the benighted and establish the enlightened—righteousness permits no objection.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo said, "You received the late emperor's dying charge and were entrusted with the altars of state; to depose the benighted and establish the enlightened—righteousness permits no objection.

sentences.zh: 但殺人二兄而以之北面，挾震主之威，據上流之重，以古推今，自免為難。」

translations.literal: But you killed his two elder brothers and set him facing north; you hold the awe of a ruler who startles his master and occupy the weight of the upper reaches—judging the present by antiquity, escape will be hard for you."
translations.idiomatic: But you killed his two elder brothers and set him on the throne; you hold the awe of a minister who startles his ruler and occupy the weight of the upper Yangzi—judging the present by antiquity, escape will be hard for you."

sentences.zh: 晦始懼不得去，既發，顧望石頭城，喜曰：「今得脫矣！」。

translations.literal: At first Hui feared he would not be allowed to leave; once he had set out he looked back toward Stone City and said with joy: "Now I have escaped!"
translations.idiomatic: At first Hui feared he would not be allowed to leave; once he had set out he looked back toward Stone City and said with joy, "Now I have escaped!"

sentences.zh: 癸卯，徐羨之進位司徒，王弘進位司空，傅亮加開府儀同三司，謝晦進號衛將軍，檀道濟進號征北將軍。。

translations.literal: On guimao Xu Xianzhi was advanced to Grand Minister, Wang Hong to Minister of Works, Fu Liang was given the open office with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies, Xie Hui was promoted to Defender General, and Tan Daoji to Northern Campaigning General.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day Xu Xianzhi was advanced to Grand Minister, Wang Hong to Minister of Works, Fu Liang was given the open office with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies, Xie Hui was promoted to Defender General, and Tan Daoji to Northern Campaigning General.

sentences.zh: 有司奏車駕依故事臨華林園聽訟。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that the imperial carriage should, according to precedent, attend at the Hualin Garden to hear lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized that the emperor should, according to precedent, attend at the Hualin Garden to hear lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「政刑多所未悉；

translations.literal: An edict said: "In government and punishments there is much I do not yet understand;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "In government and punishments there is much I do not yet understand;

sentences.zh: 可如先者，二公推訊。」。

translations.literal: what may follow precedent, let the two excellencies examine and decide."
translations.idiomatic: what may follow precedent, let the two excellencies examine and decide."

sentences.zh: 帝以王曇首、王華為侍中，曇首領右衛將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor made Wang Tanshou and Wang Hua palace attendants; Tanshou also headed the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Wang Tanshou and Wang Hua palace attendants; Tanshou also headed the right guard.

sentences.zh: 華領驍騎將軍，朱容子為右軍將軍。。

translations.literal: Hua headed the valiant cavalry, and Zhu Rongzi was made general of the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hua headed the valiant cavalry, and Zhu Rongzi was made general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，追尊帝母胡婕妤曰章皇后。

translations.literal: On jiachen the emperor's mother, Lady Hu, was posthumously honored as Empress Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day the emperor's mother, Lady Hu, was posthumously honored as Empress Zhang.

sentences.zh: 封皇弟義恭為江夏王，義宣為竟陵王，義季為衡陽王；

translations.literal: The emperor's younger brothers Yigong, Yixuan, and Yiji were enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangxia, Prince of Jingling, and Prince of Hengyang;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's younger brothers Yigong, Yixuan, and Yiji were enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangxia, Prince of Jingling, and Prince of Hengyang;

sentences.zh: 仍以義宣為左將軍，鎮石頭。。

translations.literal: Yixuan was also made Left General and stationed at Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan was also made Left General and stationed at Stone City.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之等欲即以到彥之為雍州，帝不許；

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi and the others wished at once to appoint Dao Yanzi to Yongzhou; the emperor did not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi and his colleagues wished at once to appoint Dao Yanzi to Yongzhou; the emperor did not permit it;

sentences.zh: 征彥之為中領軍，委以戎政。

translations.literal: Yanzi was summoned as director of the central guards and entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzi was summoned as director of the central guards and entrusted with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 彥之自襄陽南下，謝晦已至鎮，慮彥之不過己。

translations.literal: As Yanzi came south from Xiangyang, Xie Hui had already reached his post and feared Yanzi would not pass by him.
translations.idiomatic: As Yanzi came south from Xiangyang, Xie Hui had already reached his post and feared Yanzi would not pass through his territory.

sentences.zh: 彥之至楊口，步往江陵，深布誠款，晦亦厚自結納；

translations.literal: When Yanzi reached Yangkou he went on foot to Jiangling, laying out his sincerity in full; Hui also bound himself to him warmly;
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzi reached Yangkou he went on foot to Jiangling and laid out his sincerity in full; Hui also received him warmly;

sentences.zh: 彥之留馬及利劍、名刀以與晦，晦由此大安。。

translations.literal: Yanzi left horses, sharp swords, and famous blades with Hui, and Hui thereby grew greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzi left horses, sharp swords, and famous blades with Hui, and Hui thereby grew greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 柔然紇升蓋可汗聞魏太宗殂，將六萬騎入雲中，殺掠吏民，攻拔盛樂宮。

translations.literal: Keshenggai Khan of Rouran, hearing that Emperor Taizong of Wei had died, led sixty thousand horse into Yunzhong, killing and plundering officials and people and capturing Shengle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Keshenggai Khan of Rouran, hearing that Emperor Taizong of Wei had died, led sixty thousand cavalry into Yunzhong, killing and plundering officials and people and capturing Shengle Palace.

sentences.zh: 魏世祖自將輕騎討之，三日二夜至雲中。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu of Wei personally led light cavalry against him and in three days and two nights reached Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu of Wei personally led light cavalry against him and reached Yunzhong in three days and two nights.

sentences.zh: 紇升蓋引騎圍魏主五十餘重，騎逼馬首，相次如堵。

translations.literal: Keshenggai led his horsemen to surround the Wei ruler more than fifty ranks deep; riders pressed on the horses' heads, rank upon rank like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: Keshenggai led his horsemen to surround the Wei emperor more than fifty ranks deep; riders pressed on the horses' heads, rank upon rank like a wall.

sentences.zh: 將士大懼，魏主顏色自若，眾情乃安。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were greatly afraid; the Wei ruler's countenance was calm as ever, and the men's hearts were thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers were greatly afraid; the Wei emperor's countenance remained calm, and the men's hearts were thereby settled.

sentences.zh: 紇升蓋以弟子於陟斤為大將，魏人射殺之；

translations.literal: Keshenggai had his younger brother's son Yuzhijin as grand general; the Wei men shot and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: Keshenggai had his nephew Yuzhijin as grand general; the Wei forces shot and killed him;

sentences.zh: 紇升蓋懼，遁去。

translations.literal: Keshenggai was afraid and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Keshenggai was afraid and fled.

sentences.zh: 尚書令劉絜言於魏主曰：「大檀自恃其眾，必將復來，請俟收田畢，大發兵為二道，東西並進以討之。」

translations.literal: Liu Jie, director of the Department of State Affairs, said to the Wei ruler: "Datan relies on his numbers and will surely come again; please wait until the harvest is complete, then raise a great force in two columns advancing east and west together to attack him."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie, director of the Department of State Affairs, said to the Wei emperor, "Datan relies on his numbers and will surely come again; please wait until the harvest is complete, then raise a great force in two columns advancing east and west together to attack him."

sentences.zh: 魏主然之。。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙子，立妃袁氏為皇后；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingzi, Consort Yuan was established as empress;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingzi day, Consort Yuan was established as empress;

sentences.zh: 耽之曾孫也。。

translations.literal: she was a great-granddaughter of Yuan Danzhi.
translations.idiomatic: she was a great-granddaughter of Yuan Danzhi.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，吐谷渾威王阿柴卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Achai, Weiwang of Tuyuhun, died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Achai, Weiwang of Tuyuhun, died.

sentences.zh: 阿柴有子二十人，疾病，召諸子弟謂之曰：「先公車騎，以大業之故，捨其子拾虔而授孤；

translations.literal: Achai had twenty sons. When ill he summoned his sons and younger brothers and said to them: "Our late lord the chariot-and-horse general, for the sake of the great enterprise, set aside his son Shiqian and entrusted me;
translations.idiomatic: Achai had twenty sons. When ill he summoned his sons and younger brothers and said, "Our late lord the chariot-and-horse general, for the sake of the great enterprise, set aside his son Shiqian and entrusted me;

sentences.zh: 孤敢私於緯代而忘先君之志乎！

translations.literal: how dare I favor Weidai privately and forget our late lord's intent!
translations.idiomatic: how dare I favor Weidai privately and forget our late lord's intent!

sentences.zh: 我死，汝曹當奉慕瑰為主。」

translations.literal: When I die, you must take Mugui as lord."
translations.idiomatic: When I die, you must take Mugui as lord."

sentences.zh: 緯代者，阿柴之長子；

translations.literal: Weidai was Achai's eldest son;
translations.idiomatic: Weidai was Achai's eldest son;

sentences.zh: 慕瑰者，阿柴之母弟、叔父烏紇提之子也。

translations.literal: Mugui was the son of Achai's younger brother by the same mother and his uncle Wuheti.
translations.idiomatic: Mugui was the son of Achai's maternal younger brother and his uncle Wuheti.

sentences.zh: 阿柴又命諸子各獻一箭，取一箭授其弟慕利延使折之，慕利延折之；

translations.literal: Achai also ordered each son to present one arrow, took one arrow and gave it to his younger brother Muliyan to break; Muliyan broke it;
translations.idiomatic: Achai also ordered each son to present one arrow, took a single arrow and gave it to his younger brother Muliyan to break; Muliyan broke it;

sentences.zh: 又取十九箭使折之，慕利延不能折。

translations.literal: then took nineteen arrows and had them broken; Muliyan could not break them.
translations.idiomatic: then took nineteen arrows and had them broken together; Muliyan could not break them.

sentences.zh: 阿柴乃諭之曰：「汝曹知之乎？

translations.literal: Achai then instructed them: "Do you understand?
translations.idiomatic: Achai then instructed them, "Do you understand?

sentences.zh: 孤則易折，眾則難摧。

translations.literal: One alone is easy to break; many together are hard to destroy.
translations.idiomatic: One alone is easy to break; many together are hard to destroy.

sentences.zh: 汝曹當戮力一心，然後可以保國寧家。」

translations.literal: You must join your strength in one heart—only then can you preserve the state and secure the clan."
translations.idiomatic: You must join your strength in one heart—only then can you preserve the state and secure the clan."

sentences.zh: 言終而卒。。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking he died.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished speaking he died.

sentences.zh: 慕瑰亦有才略，撫納秦、涼失業之民及氐、羌雜種至五六百落，部眾轉盛。。

translations.literal: Mugui also had talent and strategy; he gathered and received displaced people of Qin and Liang and mixed Di and Qiang groups to the number of five or six hundred clans, and his following grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Mugui also had talent and strategy; he gathered displaced people of Qin and Liang and mixed Di and Qiang groups to the number of five or six hundred clans, and his following grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏主命安集將軍長孫翰、安北將軍尉眷北擊柔然，魏主自將屯柞山。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Wei ruler ordered the pacifying general Zhangsun Han and the northern-pacifying general Yu Juan to strike Rouran in the north; the Wei ruler personally led troops and encamped at Zhaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Wei emperor ordered the pacifying general Zhangsun Han and the northern-pacifying general Yu Juan to strike Rouran in the north; the Wei emperor personally led troops and encamped at Zhaoshan.

sentences.zh: 柔然北遁，諸軍追之，大獲而還。

translations.literal: Rouran fled north; the armies pursued and returned with great gains.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran fled north; the armies pursued and returned with great gains.

sentences.zh: 翰，肥之子也。。

translations.literal: Han was a son of Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Han was a son of Zhangsun Fei.

sentences.zh: 詔拜營陽王母張氏為營陽太妃。。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Lady Zhang, mother of the Prince of Yingyang, as Grand Princess of Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Lady Zhang, mother of the Prince of Yingyang, Grand Princess of Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 林邑王范陽邁寇日南、九德諸郡。。

translations.literal: Fan Yangmai, King of Linyi, raided Rinan and the commanderies of Jiude and others.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yangmai, king of Linyi, raided Rinan and the commanderies of Jiude and others.

sentences.zh: 宕昌王梁彌匆遣子彌黃入見於魏。

translations.literal: Liang Michong, King of Dangchang, sent his son Mihuang to appear before Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Michong, King of Dangchang, sent his son Mihuang to pay court to Wei.

sentences.zh: 宕昌，羌之別種也。

translations.literal: Dangchang is a separate branch of the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dangchang was a separate branch of the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 羌地東接中國，西通西域，長數千里，各有酋帥，部落分地，不相統攝；

translations.literal: Qiang territory adjoins China on the east and connects with the Western Regions on the west, extending several thousand li; each has its own chieftain, tribes dividing land among themselves, not united under one authority;
translations.idiomatic: Qiang lands adjoined China on the east and reached the Western Regions on the west, stretching several thousand li; each had its own chieftain, tribes holding separate territories without a single overlord;

sentences.zh: 而宕昌最強，有民二萬餘落，諸種畏之。。

translations.literal: but Dangchang is strongest, with more than twenty thousand clans of people, and the various tribes fear it.
translations.idiomatic: but Dangchang was the strongest, with more than twenty thousand clans, and the other tribes feared it.

sentences.zh: 夏主將廢太子瑰而立少子酒泉公倫。

translations.literal: The ruler of Xia was about to depose the crown prince Gui and install his youngest son, the Duke of Jiuquan Lun.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler was about to depose Crown Prince Gui and install his youngest son, Duke Lun of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 瑰聞之，將兵七萬北伐倫。

translations.literal: Gui heard of it and led seventy thousand troops north to attack Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Gui heard of it and marched north with seventy thousand troops to attack Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫將騎三萬拒之，戰於高平，倫敗死。

translations.literal: Lun led thirty thousand cavalry to resist; they fought at Gaoping, and Lun was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lun mustered thirty thousand cavalry to resist; they fought at Gaoping, and Lun was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 倫兄太原公昌將騎一萬襲瑰，殺之，並其眾八萬五千，歸於統萬。

translations.literal: Lun's elder brother Chang, Duke of Taiyuan, led ten thousand cavalry to attack Gui, killed him, merged his force of eighty-five thousand, and returned to Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's elder brother Chang, Duke of Taiyuan, led ten thousand cavalry against Gui, killed him, absorbed his eighty-five thousand men, and returned to Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 夏主大悅，立昌為太子。

translations.literal: The ruler of Xia was greatly pleased and established Chang as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler was greatly pleased and made Chang crown prince.

sentences.zh: 夏主好自矜大，名其四門：東曰招魏，南曰朝宋，西曰服涼，北曰平朔。。

translations.literal: The ruler of Xia was fond of self-aggrandizement; he named his four gates: the east was called Summoning Wei, the south Attending Song, the west Subduing Liang, and the north Pacifying the North.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler loved to boast of his greatness; he named his four gates Summoning Wei to the east, Attending Song to the south, Subduing Liang to the west, and Pacifying the North to the north.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之上元嘉二年（乙丑，公元四二五年） 。

translations.literal: Above, second part of the reign of Emperor Wen the Literary: Yuanjia year 2 (yichou; 425 CE).
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 2, second year of the reign of Emperor Wen—above, part one (yichou; 425 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，徐羨之、傅亮上表歸政，表三上，帝乃許之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang submitted memorials returning power; the memorial was submitted three times, and the emperor then permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang submitted memorials returning power to the throne; after three submissions the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，始親萬機。

translations.literal: On bingyin he began personally to attend to the myriad affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day he began personally to attend to affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 羨之仍遜位還第，徐佩之、程道惠及吳興太守王韶之等並謂非宜，敦勸甚苦，乃復奉詔視事。。

translations.literal: Xianzhi still yielded his post and returned home; Xu Peizhi, Cheng Daohui, and Wang Shaozhi, governor of Wuxing, all said it was not fitting and urged him strenuously; he then again received the edict and resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi still resigned and returned home; Xu Peizhi, Cheng Daohui, and Wang Shaozhi, governor of Wuxing, all said it was wrong and pressed him hard; he then accepted the edict and resumed office.

sentences.zh: 辛未，帝祀南郊，大赦。。

translations.literal: On xinwei the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己卯，魏主還平城。。

translations.literal: On jimao the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 二月，燕有女子化為男。

translations.literal: In the second month, in Yan a woman transformed into a man.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month a woman in Yan transformed into a man.

sentences.zh: 燕主以問群臣，沿書左丞傅權對曰：「西漢之末，雌雞化為雄，猶有王莽之禍。

translations.literal: The ruler of Yan asked his ministers; Fu Quan, left assistant director of the Secretariat, replied: "At the end of Western Han, hens transformed into roosters, and still there was Wang Mang's disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan ruler asked his ministers; Fu Quan, left assistant director of the Secretariat, replied, "At the end of Western Han, hens turned into roosters, and still Wang Mang's disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 況今女化為男，臣將為君之兆也。」。

translations.literal: How much more now that a woman has transformed into a man—this is an omen that your subject will become ruler."
translations.idiomatic: How much more now that a woman has become a man—this is an omen that your subject will become ruler."

sentences.zh: 三月，丙寅，魏主尊保母竇氏為保太后。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingyin, the Wei ruler honored his foster mother Lady Dou as Grand Empress Dowager of Fostering.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingyin day, the Wei ruler honored his foster mother Lady Dou as Grand Empress Dowager of Fostering.

sentences.zh: 密後之殂也，世祖尚幼，太宗以竇氏慈良，有操行，使保養之。

translations.literal: When Empress Mi died, Shizu was still young; Emperor Taizong, because Lady Dou was kind and good and possessed moral conduct, had her nurture and raise him.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Mi died, Shizu was still young; Emperor Taizong, finding Lady Dou kind, good, and upright in conduct, entrusted her with his upbringing.

sentences.zh: 竇氏撫視有恩，訓導有禮，世神德之，故加以尊號，奉養不異所在。。

translations.literal: Lady Dou nursed and watched over him with kindness, instructed and guided him with propriety; Shizu held her in virtue for this, and therefore added to her an honorific title, maintaining her in the same manner as before wherever she was.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Dou cared for him with affection and guided him with propriety; Shizu held her in gratitude and therefore bestowed on her an honorific title, maintaining her support as before wherever she resided.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，魏以長孫嵩為太尉，長孫翰為司徒，奚斤為司空。。

translations.literal: On disi Wei appointed Zhangsun Song Grand Minister, Zhangsun Han Minister over the Masses, and Xi Jin Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On disi day Wei appointed Zhangsun Song Grand Minister, Zhangsun Han Minister over the Masses, and Xi Jin Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，秦王熾磐遣平遠將軍叱盧犍等，襲河西鎮南將軍沮渠白蹄於臨松，擒之，徙其民五千餘戶於枹罕。。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Qifu Chipan, King of Qin, sent the distant-pacifying general Chilu Jian and others to attack the southern-pacifying general of Hexi Juqu Baiti at Linsong, captured him, and moved more than five thousand households to Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Qifu Chipan, King of Qin, sent the distant-pacifying general Chilu Jian and others to attack Juqu Baiti, southern-pacifying general of Hexi, at Linsong, captured him, and relocated more than five thousand households to Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣龍驤將軍步堆等來聘，始復通好。。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler sent the dragon-charger general Bu Dui and others on a friendly mission, and good relations were restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler sent the dragon-charger general Bu Dui and others on a friendly mission, restoring diplomatic ties.

sentences.zh: 六月，武都惠文王楊盛卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yang Sheng, Cultured Literary King of Wudu, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yang Sheng, the Cultured Literary King of Wudu, died.

sentences.zh: 初，盛聞晉亡，不改義熙年號，謂世子玄曰：「吾老矣，當終為晉臣，汝善事宋帝。」

translations.literal: Previously, when Sheng heard that Jin had perished, he did not change the Yixi era name; he said to his heir Xuan: "I am old; I shall remain a subject of Jin to the end—you serve the Emperor of Song well."
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when Sheng heard that Jin had fallen, he kept the Yixi era name unchanged; he told his heir Xuan, "I am old; I shall die a subject of Jin—you serve the Song emperor well."

sentences.zh: 及盛卒，玄自稱都督隴右諸軍事、征西大將軍、開府儀同三司、秦州刺史、武都王，遣使來告喪，始用元喜年號。。

translations.literal: When Sheng died, Xuan styled himself director of all military affairs of Longyou, great general on the western campaign, open office with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies, governor of Qinzhou, and King of Wudu; he sent envoys to announce the death and only then adopted the Yuanshi era name.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng died, Xuan took the titles director of all military affairs of Longyou, great general on the western campaign, open office with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies, governor of Qinzhou, and King of Wudu; he sent envoys to announce the death and only then adopted the Yuanshi era name.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，秦王熾磐鎮南將軍吉毘等南擊黑水羌酋丘擔，大破之。。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Qifu Chipan's southern-pacifying general Ji Pi and others attacked Qiu Dan, chieftain of the Black Water Qiang, to the south and routed him thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Qifu Chipan's southern-pacifying general Ji Pi and others attacked Qiu Dan, chieftain of the Black Water Qiang, to the south and routed him thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 八月，夏武烈帝殂，葬嘉平陵，廟號世祖；

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Martial Fierce Emperor of Xia died, was buried at Jiaping Mausoleum, and given the temple name Shizu;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Martial Fierce Emperor of Xia died, was buried at Jiaping Mausoleum, and received the temple name Shizu;

sentences.zh: 太子昌即皇帝位。

translations.literal: the crown prince Chang took the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Chang ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元承光。。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Chengguang.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Chengguang.

sentences.zh: 王弘自以始不預定策，不受司空；

translations.literal: Wang Hong, because he had from the first not participated in the decisive plot, would not accept the post of Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, because he had not taken part in the original plot, refused the post of Minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 表讓彌年，乃許之。

translations.literal: he submitted declining it year after year, and only then was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: he submitted memorials declining it year after year before permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以弘為車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。。

translations.literal: On yiyou Hong was made chariot-and-horse general with open office and ritual equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day Hong was made chariot-and-horse general with open office and ritual equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丘擔以其眾降秦，秦以擔為歸善將軍；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Qiu Dan surrendered with his followers to Qin; Qin made Dan General Who Returns to Goodness;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Qiu Dan surrendered with his followers to Qin; Qin made him General Who Returns to Goodness;

sentences.zh: 拜折衝將軍乞伏信帝為平羌校尉以鎮之。。

translations.literal: and appointed the breaking-campaign general Qifu Xindi as colonel pacifying the Qiang to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed the breaking-campaign general Qifu Xindi colonel pacifying the Qiang to garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，魏主大舉伐柔然，五道並進。

translations.literal: On guimao the Wei ruler launched a major campaign against Rouran, five columns advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day the Wei ruler launched a major campaign against Rouran, five columns advancing together.

sentences.zh: 長孫翰等從東道出黑漠，廷尉卿長孫道生等出白、黑二漠之間，魏主從中道，東平公娥清出栗園，奚斤等從西道，出爾寒山。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Han and others went by the eastern route through the Black Desert; Court Director Zhangsun Daosheng and others emerged between the White and Black deserts; the Wei ruler took the middle route; Duke of Dongping E Qing went out from Liyuan; Xi Jin and others took the western route, emerging from Erhanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Han and others took the eastern route through the Black Desert; Court Director Zhangsun Daosheng and others emerged between the White and Black deserts; the Wei ruler took the middle route; Duke of Dongping E Qing went out from Liyuan; Xi Jin and others took the western route from Erhanshan.

sentences.zh: 諸軍至漠南，捨輜重，輕騎，繼十五日糧，度漠擊之。

translations.literal: When the armies reached south of the desert they abandoned baggage trains, took light cavalry, carried fifteen days' rations, crossed the desert, and struck.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies reached the southern desert they abandoned baggage trains, traveled light with fifteen days' rations, crossed the desert, and attacked.

sentences.zh: 柔然部落大驚，絕跡北走。。

translations.literal: The Rouran tribes were greatly alarmed and fled north without a trace.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran tribes were thrown into panic and fled north without a trace.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以武都世子玄為北秦州刺史、武都王。。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the heir of Wudu Xuan was made governor of North Qinzhou and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Wudu's heir Xuan was made governor of North Qinzhou and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 初，會稽孔寧子為帝鎮西咨議參軍，及即位，以寧子為步兵校尉；

translations.literal: Previously, Kong Ningzi of Kuaiji had been the prince's western-staff advisory aide; when the emperor took the throne he made Ningzi commandant of the infantry;
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Kong Ningzi of Kuaiji had served as the prince's western-staff advisory aide; when the emperor took the throne he made Ningzi commandant of the infantry;

sentences.zh: 與侍中王華並有富貴之願，疾徐羨之、傅亮專權，日夜構之於帝。

translations.literal: Kong and Palace Attendant Wang Hua both harbored ambitions for wealth and rank; they resented Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang for monopolizing power and day and night wove plots against them before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Kong and Palace Attendant Wang Hua both coveted wealth and rank; they resented Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang for monopolizing power and day and night whispered against them to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會謝晦二女當適彭城王義康、新野侯義賓，遣其妻曹氏及長子世休送女至建康。

translations.literal: It happened that two daughters of Xie Hui were to marry Prince Yikang of Pengcheng and Marquis Yibin of Xinye; he sent his wife Lady Cao and his eldest son Shixiu to escort the daughters to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that two daughters of Xie Hui were to marry Prince Yikang of Pengcheng and Marquis Yibin of Xinye; he sent his wife Lady Cao and his eldest son Shixiu to escort the brides to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 帝欲誅羨之、亮，並發兵討晦，聲言當伐魏，取河南，又言拜京陵，治行裝艦。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to execute Xianzhi and Liang and also dispatch troops to suppress Hui; he gave out that he would attack Wei and take Henan, and also spoke of visiting the capital tombs, fitting out traveling vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to execute Xianzhi and Liang and also dispatch troops against Hui; he gave out that he would attack Wei and recover Henan, and also spoke of visiting the imperial tombs and fitting out transport ships.

sentences.zh: 亮與晦書曰：「薄伐河朔，事猶未已，朝野之慮，憂懼者多。」

translations.literal: Liang wrote to Hui: "The slight campaign into the north of the river is still not concluded; throughout court and realm anxiety and fear are many."
translations.idiomatic: Liang wrote to Hui, "The punitive expedition into the north of the river is still unfinished; throughout court and country anxiety runs high."

sentences.zh: 又言：「朝士多諫北征，上當遣外監萬幼宗往相咨訪。」

translations.literal: He also wrote: "Court gentlemen have mostly remonstrated against the northern expedition; the emperor is likely to send Chief Surveillance Officer Wan Youzong to consult."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Court gentlemen have mostly remonstrated against the northern expedition; the emperor is likely to send Chief Surveillance Officer Wan Youzong to consult."

sentences.zh: 時朝廷處分異常，其謀頗洩。。

translations.literal: At this time the court's dispositions were unusual, and the plot leaked rather openly.
translations.idiomatic: By then the court's movements were unusual, and the plot leaked rather openly.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之上元嘉三年（丙寅，公元四二六年） 。

translations.literal: Above, third part of the reign of Emperor Wen the Literary: Yuanjia year 3 (bingyin; 426 CE).
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 3, third year of the reign of Emperor Wen—above, part one (bingyin; 426 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，謝晦弟黃門侍郎㬭馳使告晦，晦猶謂不然，以傅亮書示咨議參軍何承天曰；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Zhan, younger brother of Xie Hui and palace attendant at the yellow gate, sent a messenger at full speed to inform Hui; Hui still thought it was not so, and showed Fu Liang's letter to the advisory aide He Chengtian, saying;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Zhan, younger brother of Xie Hui and palace attendant at the yellow gate, sent a messenger at full speed to warn Hui; Hui still disbelieved it and showed Fu Liang's letter to the advisory aide He Chengtian, saying;

sentences.zh: 「計幼宗一二日必至。

translations.literal: "I reckon Youzong will arrive in a day or two.
translations.idiomatic: "Youzong should arrive within a day or two.

sentences.zh: 傅公慮我好事，故先遣此書。」

translations.literal: Master Fu feared I would stir trouble, and therefore sent this letter first."
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu feared I would make trouble, and therefore sent this letter first."

sentences.zh: 承天曰：「外間所聞，鹹謂西討已定，幼宗豈有上理！」

translations.literal: Chengtian said: "What is heard outside all says the western expedition is settled—how could Youzong have grounds to come upriver!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian said, "What is heard outside is that the western expedition is settled—how could Youzong have reason to come upriver!"

sentences.zh: 晦尚謂虛妄，使承天豫立答詔啟草，言伐虜宜須明年。

translations.literal: Hui still considered it empty talk and had Chengtian prepare in advance a draft reply to the imperial edict, saying an attack on the barbarians should wait until next year.
translations.idiomatic: Hui still thought it empty talk and had Chengtian prepare in advance a draft reply to the imperial edict, saying the barbarian campaign should wait until next year.

sentences.zh: 江夏內史程道惠得尋陽人書，言「朝廷將有大處分，其事已審」，使其輔國府中兵參軍樂冏封以示晦。

translations.literal: Cheng Daohui, internal administrator of Jiangxia, received a letter from a man of Xunyang saying "the court is about to take drastic measures—the matter is already settled"; he had his aide-de-camp Yue Tong of the Protectorate of the State seal it and show it to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Daohui, internal administrator of Jiangxia, received a letter from a man of Xunyang saying "the court is about to take drastic measures—the matter is already settled"; he had Yue Tong, aide-de-camp of the Protectorate of the State, seal it and show it to Hui.

sentences.zh: 晦問承天曰：「若果爾，卿令我雲何？」

translations.literal: Hui asked Chengtian: "If it is really so, what do you tell me to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui asked Chengtian, "If it is really so, what do you tell me to do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「蒙將軍殊顧，常思報德。

translations.literal: He replied: "I have received the general's especial regard and always think to repay your kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have received the general's especial regard and always think to repay your kindness.

sentences.zh: 事變至矣，何敢隱情！

translations.literal: The crisis has arrived—how dare I conceal the truth!
translations.idiomatic: The crisis is upon us—how dare I hide what I know!

sentences.zh: 然明日戒嚴，動用軍法，區區所懷，懼不得盡。」

translations.literal: Yet if tomorrow there is martial alert and military law is invoked, what I hold in my heart, I fear I cannot express fully."
translations.idiomatic: But if tomorrow there is martial alert and military law is invoked, what little I can say here may not be enough."

sentences.zh: 晦懼曰：「卿豈欲我自裁邪？」

translations.literal: Hui, afraid, said: "Do you wish me to take my own life?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui, afraid, said, "Do you wish me to take my own life?"

sentences.zh: 承天曰：「尚未至此。

translations.literal: Chengtian said: "It has not yet come to that.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian said, "It has not yet come to that.

sentences.zh: 以王者之重，舉天下以攻一州，大小既殊，逆順又異。

translations.literal: With the weight of an emperor's position, to raise all under Heaven to attack one province—the scale is already unequal, and right and wrong likewise differ.
translations.idiomatic: With the weight of an emperor's throne, to raise all under Heaven against one province—the scale is already unequal, and right and wrong likewise differ.

sentences.zh: 境外求全，上計也。

translations.literal: To seek safety beyond the borders is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking safety beyond the borders is the best course.

sentences.zh: 其次以腹心將兵屯義陽，將軍自帥大眾戰於夏口；

translations.literal: Next best is to have trusted generals garrison troops at Yiyang while the general himself leads the main force to fight at Xiakou;
translations.idiomatic: Next best is to have trusted generals garrison troops at Yiyang while you yourself lead the main force to fight at Xiakou;

sentences.zh: 若敗，即趨義陽以出北境，其次也。」

translations.literal: if defeated, then hurry to Yiyang and exit through the northern frontier—that is the second plan."
