translations.idiomatic: if defeated, hurry to Yiyang and break out through the northern frontier—that is the second-best course."

sentences.zh: 晦良久曰：「荊州用武之地，兵糧易給，聊且決戰，走復何晚！」

translations.literal: After a long while Hui said: "Jingzhou is a land for wielding arms; troops and grain are easy to supply—a battle first, and flight would come none too late!"
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Hui said, "Jingzhou is a land made for war; troops and grain are easy to supply—we can fight first, and flight would come none too late!"

sentences.zh: 乃使承天造立表檄，又與衛軍咨議參軍琅邪顏邵謀舉兵，邵飲藥而死。。

translations.literal: He then had Chengtian draft manifestos and memorials, and also consulted with the defender-general's advisory aide Yan Shao of Langya about raising troops; Shao drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Chengtian draft manifestos and memorials, and also consulted with the defender-general's advisory aide Yan Shao of Langya about raising troops; Shao took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 晦立幡戒嚴，謂司馬庾登之曰：「今當自下，欲屈卿以三千人守城，備御劉粹。」

translations.literal: Hui raised banners and declared martial alert; he said to Chief Administrator Yu Dengzhi: "We are about to go downstream; I wish to impose on you to hold the city with three thousand men and guard against Liu Cui."
translations.idiomatic: Hui raised banners and declared martial alert; he said to Chief Administrator Yu Dengzhi, "We are about to go downstream; I wish to impose on you to hold the city with three thousand men and guard against Liu Cui."

sentences.zh: 登之曰：「下官親老在都，又素無部眾，情計二三，不敢受此旨。」

translations.literal: Dengzhi said: "This subordinate's aged parents are in the capital, and I have never had troops under my command; my heart wavers in two or three ways—I dare not accept this commission."
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi said, "My aged parents are in the capital, and I have never had troops under my command; my heart wavers—I dare not accept this commission."

sentences.zh: 晦仍問諸將佐：「戰士三千足守城否？」

translations.literal: Hui then asked the officers: "Are three thousand warriors enough to hold the city?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui then asked the officers, "Are three thousand warriors enough to hold the city?"

sentences.zh: 南蠻司馬周超對曰：「非徒守城而已，若有外寇，可以立功。」

translations.literal: Southern Barbarian Chief Administrator Zhou Chao replied: "Not merely to hold the city—if there is an external enemy, one can win merit."
translations.idiomatic: Southern Barbarian Chief Administrator Zhou Chao replied, "Not merely to hold the city—if an external enemy comes, one can win merit."

sentences.zh: 登之因曰：「超必能力，下官請解司馬、南郡以授之。」

translations.literal: Dengzhi thereupon said: "Chao is surely capable; this subordinate asks to resign as chief administrator and as governor of Nanjun and confer them on him."
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi thereupon said, "Chao is surely capable; I ask to resign as chief administrator and governor of Nanjun and confer both posts on him."

sentences.zh: 晦即於坐命超為司馬，領南義陽太守；

translations.literal: Hui then, right there in the assembly, appointed Chao chief administrator and acting governor of Southern Yiyang;
translations.idiomatic: Hui then appointed Chao chief administrator on the spot and made him acting governor of Southern Yiyang;

sentences.zh: 轉登之為長史，南郡如故。

translations.literal: he transferred Dengzhi to chief clerk, retaining Nanjun as before.
translations.idiomatic: he transferred Dengzhi to chief clerk while keeping him governor of Nanjun as before.

sentences.zh: 登之，蘊之孫也。。

translations.literal: Dengzhi was a grandson of Yunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi was a grandson of Yu Yunzhi.

sentences.zh: 帝以王弘、檀道濟始不預廢弒之謀，弘弟曇首又為帝所親委，事將發，密使報弘，且召道濟，欲使討晦。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Wang Hong and Tan Daoji had from the start not participated in the plot to depose and murder the princes, and Hong's younger brother Tanshou was also personally entrusted by the Emperor—as matters were about to break, secretly sent messengers to inform Hong and also summoned Daoji, intending to have him campaign against Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew that Wang Hong and Tan Daoji had never been part of the plot to depose and kill the princes, and that Hong's younger brother Tanshou enjoyed his personal trust. As the crisis approached, he secretly sent word to Hong and summoned Daoji, intending to send him against Xie Hui.

sentences.zh: 王華等皆以為不可，帝曰：「道濟止於脅從，本非創謀。

translations.literal: Wang Hua and the others all said it was inadvisable. The Emperor said: "Daoji was only coerced into following; he was not originally the author of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua and the others all said it was inadvisable. The Emperor said, "Daoji was only coerced into following; he was not originally the author of the plot.

sentences.zh: 殺害之事，又所不關。

translations.literal: The matter of the killings, moreover, did not involve him.
translations.idiomatic: The killings, moreover, did not involve him at all.

sentences.zh: 吾撫而使之，必將無慮。」

translations.literal: If I comfort him and employ him, there will surely be no cause for worry."
translations.idiomatic: If I reassure him and put him to use, there will be nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 乙丑，道濟至建康。。

translations.literal: On yichou, Daoji arrived at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Daoji arrived at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，下詔暴羨之、亮、晦殺營陽、廬陵王之罪，命有司誅之，且曰：「晦據有上流，或不即罪，朕當親帥六師為其過防。

translations.literal: On bingyin, an edict was issued exposing the crimes of Xianzhi, Liang, and Hui in killing the Princes of Yingyang and Luling, ordering the relevant offices to execute them, and saying: "Hui holds the upper Yangtze; he may not immediately submit to judgment—I shall personally lead the six armies to guard against his crossing.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, an edict was issued exposing the crimes of Xianzhi, Liang, and Hui in killing the Princes of Yingyang and Luling, ordering the proper offices to execute them, and declaring: "Hui holds the upper Yangtze; he may not submit at once—I shall personally lead the six armies to block his crossing.

sentences.zh: 可遣中領軍在彥之即日電發，征北將軍檀道濟駱驛繼路，符衛軍府州，以時收翦，已命雍州刺史劉粹等斷其走伏。

translations.literal: The Central Army Inspector Dao Yanzhi may be dispatched to set out this very day by forced march; the Northern Expedition General Tan Daoji is to follow in rapid relays along the route; orders go to the Defender-General's offices and the provinces to cut them down in timely fashion; Liu Cui, governor of Yong Province, and others have already been ordered to cut off his routes of flight and hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch the Central Army Inspector Dao Yanzhi to set out at once by forced march; the Northern Expedition General Tan Daoji is to follow in rapid relays along the route; send orders to the Defender-General's offices and the provinces to destroy them without delay; Liu Cui, governor of Yong Province, and others have already been ordered to cut off every route of escape.

sentences.zh: 罪止元兇，餘無所問。」。

translations.literal: Punishment is limited to the chief culprits; no others will be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: Punishment is limited to the ringleaders; no one else will be questioned."

sentences.zh: 是日，詔召羨之、亮。

translations.literal: That same day, an edict summoned Xianzhi and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, an edict summoned Xianzhi and Liang.

sentences.zh: 羨之行至西明門外，謝㬭正直，遣報亮云：「殿內有異處分。」

translations.literal: Xianzhi, as he proceeded to outside the Ximing Gate, met Xie Yan on duty; he sent word to Liang, saying: "There is an unusual disposition within the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi, on his way to outside the Ximing Gate, met Xie Yan on duty and sent word to Liang: "There is an unusual disposition within the palace."

sentences.zh: 亮辭以嫂病暫還，遣信報羨之，羨之還西州，乘內人問訊車出郭，步走至新林，入陶灶中自經死。

translations.literal: Liang declined on the pretext that his sister-in-law was ill and he needed to return briefly; he sent a messenger to report to Xianzhi. Xianzhi returned to Xizhou, took an inner-court inquiry carriage out of the city, walked on foot to Xinlin, entered a pottery kiln, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liang pleaded that his sister-in-law was ill and he must return briefly; he sent a messenger to warn Xianzhi. Xianzhi went back to Xizhou, rode an inner-court inquiry carriage out of the city, walked on foot to Xinlin, entered a pottery kiln, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 亮乘車出郭門，乘馬奔兄迪墓，屯騎校尉郭泓收之。

translations.literal: Liang rode out in a carriage through the city gate, mounted a horse, and galloped to his elder brother Di's tomb; Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Guo Hong seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang rode out through the city gate in a carriage, then mounted a horse and galloped to his elder brother Di's tomb; Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Guo Hong seized him.

sentences.zh: 至廣莫門，上遣中書舍人以詔書示亮，並謂曰：「以公江陵之誠，當使諸子無恙。」

translations.literal: At the Guangmo Gate, the Emperor sent a Palace Secretariat Attendant to show Liang the edict, and also said: "In consideration of your loyalty at Jiangling, your sons shall be kept unharmed."
translations.idiomatic: At the Guangmo Gate, the Emperor sent a Palace Secretariat Attendant to show Liang the edict and added: "In view of your loyalty at Jiangling, your sons shall come to no harm."

sentences.zh: 亮讀詔書訖，曰：「亮受先帝布衣之眷，遂蒙顧托。

translations.literal: After reading the edict through, Liang said: "I received the late Emperor's favor when he was still in common dress, and thus received his dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: After reading the edict through, Liang said, "I received the late Emperor's favor when he was still in common dress, and thus received his dying charge.

sentences.zh: 黜昏立明，社稷之計也。

translations.literal: To remove the dim and establish the bright—that was a plan for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: To remove the dim and establish the bright—that was a plan for the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 欲加之罪，其無辭乎！」

translations.literal: If you wish to attach guilt to me, is there no pretext!"
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to attach guilt to me, is there no pretext!"

sentences.zh: 於是誅亮而徙其妻子於建安；

translations.literal: Thereupon Liang was executed and his wife and children were exiled to Jian'an;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Liang was executed and his wife and children were exiled to Jian'an;

sentences.zh: 誅羨之二子，而宥其兄子佩之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's two sons were executed, but his elder brother's son Peizhi was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's two sons were executed, but his elder brother's son Peizhi was spared.

sentences.zh: 誅晦子世休，收系謝㬭。。

translations.literal: Hui's son Shixiu was executed, and Xie Yan was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's son Shixiu was executed, and Xie Yan was arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 帝將討謝晦，問策於檀道濟，對曰：「臣昔與晦同從北征，入關十策，晦有其九，才略明練，殆為少敵。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to campaign against Xie Hui and asked Tan Daoji for strategy. He replied: "Your servant once campaigned north with Hui; of the ten stratagems for entering the pass, Hui had nine—his talent and design are clear and practiced; he has scarcely an equal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was about to campaign against Xie Hui and asked Tan Daoji for strategy. He replied, "Your servant once campaigned north with Hui; of the ten stratagems for entering the pass, Hui had nine—his talent and design are clear and practiced; he has scarcely an equal.

sentences.zh: 然未嘗孤軍決勝，戎事恐非其長。

translations.literal: Yet he has never won decisive victory with an isolated army; military affairs are probably not his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he has never won decisive victory with an isolated army; military affairs are probably not his strength.

sentences.zh: 臣悉晦智，晦悉臣勇。

translations.literal: I know Hui's intelligence completely; Hui knows my courage completely.
translations.idiomatic: I know Hui's intelligence completely; Hui knows my courage completely.

sentences.zh: 今奉王命以討之，可未陳而擒也。」

translations.literal: Now, receiving Your Majesty's command to campaign against him, he can be captured before battle is even joined."
translations.idiomatic: Now, receiving Your Majesty's command to campaign against him, he can be captured before battle is even joined."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，征王弘為侍中、司徒、錄尚書事、揚州刺史，以彭城王義康為都督荊、湘等八州諸軍事、荊州刺史。。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Wang Hong was summoned as Palace Attendant, Grand Mentor, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and governor of Yang Province; Prince Pengcheng Yikang was made commander-in-chief of military affairs over Jing, Xiang, and seven other provinces, and governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Wang Hong was summoned as Palace Attendant, Grand Mentor, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and governor of Yang Province; Prince Pengcheng Yikang was made commander-in-chief of military affairs over Jing, Xiang, and seven other provinces, and governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 樂冏復遣使告謝晦以徐、傅及㬭等已誅。

translations.literal: Yue Tong again sent envoys to inform Xie Hui that Xu, Fu, Yan, and the others had already been executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Tong again sent envoys to inform Xie Hui that Xu, Fu, Yan, and the others had already been executed.

sentences.zh: 晦先舉羨之、亮哀，次發子弟凶問，既而自出射堂勒兵。

translations.literal: Hui first observed mourning for Xianzhi and Liang, then issued notifications of the violent deaths of kinsmen; afterward he personally went to the archery hall to muster troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hui first observed mourning for Xianzhi and Liang, then issued notifications of the violent deaths of kinsmen; afterward he personally went to the archery hall to muster troops.

sentences.zh: 晦從高祖征討，指麾處分，莫不曲盡其宜，數日間，四遠投集，得精兵三萬人。

translations.literal: Hui had followed the Founding Emperor on campaigns; in command and disposition nothing fell short of the apt—within a few days men gathered from far and near, and he obtained thirty thousand elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had followed the Founding Emperor on campaign; in command and disposition his measures were always exactly right—within days men rallied from far and near, and he raised thirty thousand elite troops.

sentences.zh: 乃奉表稱羨之、亮等忠貞，橫被冤酷。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial declaring Xianzhi, Liang, and the others loyal and true, cruelly and wrongfully condemned.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial declaring Xianzhi, Liang, and the others loyal and true, cruelly and wrongfully condemned.

sentences.zh: 且言：「臣等若志欲執權，不專為國，初廢營陽，陛下在遠，武皇之子尚有童幼，擁以號令，誰敢非之！

translations.literal: And he said: "If we truly wished to seize power and did not act solely for the state, when Yingyang was first deposed, Your Majesty was far away, and among Emperor Wu's sons there were still young children—if we had gathered them and issued orders in their name, who would have dared oppose us!
translations.idiomatic: And he said, "If we truly wished to seize power and did not act solely for the state, when Yingyang was first deposed, Your Majesty was far away, and among Emperor Wu's sons there were still young children—if we had gathered them and issued orders in their name, who would have dared oppose us!

sentences.zh: 豈得溯流三千里，虛館七旬，仰望鸞旗者哉！

translations.literal: How could we have traveled upstream three thousand li, lodged in empty halls for seventy days, gazing up at the imperial banners!
translations.idiomatic: How could we have traveled upstream three thousand li, lodged in empty halls for seventy days, gazing up at the imperial banners!

sentences.zh: 故廬陵王，於營陽之世積怨犯上，自貽非命。

translations.literal: The late Prince of Luling, in the reign of Yingyang, accumulated grievances and offended his sovereign—he brought ruin upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: The late Prince of Luling, in the reign of Yingyang, accumulated grievances and offended his sovereign—he brought ruin upon himself.

sentences.zh: 不有所廢，將何以興！

translations.literal: If one does not remove some, how can one raise up others!
translations.idiomatic: If one does not remove some, how can one raise up others!

sentences.zh: 耿弇不以賊遺君、父，臣亦何負於宋室邪！

translations.literal: Geng Yan did not leave rebels to his lord and father—what debt do I owe the House of Song!
translations.idiomatic: Geng Yan did not leave rebels to his lord and father—what debt do I owe the House of Song!

sentences.zh: 此皆王弘、王曇首、王華險躁猜忌，讒構成禍。

translations.literal: All this is because Wang Hong, Wang Tanshou, and Wang Hua are rash, jealous, and suspicious—they slandered and brought calamity.
translations.idiomatic: All this is because Wang Hong, Wang Tanshou, and Wang Hua are rash, jealous, and suspicious—they slandered and brought calamity.

sentences.zh: 今當舉兵以除君側之惡。」。

translations.literal: Now we must raise troops to remove the evil at the ruler's side."
translations.idiomatic: Now we must raise troops to remove the evil at the ruler's side."

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐復遣使如魏，請用師於夏。。

translations.literal: King Qiwu Chiqian of Qin again sent envoys to Wei, requesting to deploy troops against Xia.
translations.idiomatic: King Qiwu Chiqian of Qin again sent envoys to Wei, requesting to deploy troops against Xia.

sentences.zh: 初，袁皇后生皇子劭，後自詳視，使馳白帝曰：「此兒形貌異常，必破國亡家，不可舉。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Empress Yuan bore the prince Shao; afterward she examined him closely and sent a fast rider to tell the Emperor: "This child's appearance is abnormal; he will surely ruin the state and destroy the family—he must not be made heir."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Yuan bore the prince Shao; afterward she examined him closely and sent a fast rider to tell the Emperor, "This child's appearance is abnormal; he will surely ruin the state and destroy the family—he must not be made heir."

sentences.zh: 即欲殺之。

translations.literal: She immediately wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: She immediately wished to kill him.

sentences.zh: 帝狼狽至後殿戶外，手撥幔禁之，乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor hurried in disarray to outside the rear hall door, pushed aside the curtain with his hand and forbade it, and only then was she stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hurried in disarray to outside the rear hall door, pushed aside the curtain with his hand and forbade it, and only then was she stopped.

sentences.zh: 以尚在諒暗，故秘之。

translations.literal: Because he was still in mourning seclusion, he kept it secret.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was still in mourning seclusion, he kept it secret.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丙戌，始言劭生。。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on bingxu, the birth of Shao was first announced.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on bingxu, the birth of Shao was first announced.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔戒嚴，大赦，諸軍相次進路以討謝晦。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict of martial alert and a general amnesty; the armies advanced in succession to campaign against Xie Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued an edict of martial alert and a general amnesty; the armies advanced in succession to campaign against Xie Hui.

sentences.zh: 晦以弟遯為竟陵內史，將萬人總留任，帥眾二萬發江陵，列舟艦自江津至於破塚，旌旗蔽日，歎曰：「恨不得以此為勤王之師！」。

translations.literal: Hui appointed his younger brother Dun interior minister of Jingling, left ten thousand men under him for overall retention duties, and led twenty thousand men from Jiangling; he arrayed ships from the Jiang crossing to Pozhong—the banners blotted out the sun—and sighed: "I only regret that these cannot serve as an army to rescue the throne!"
translations.idiomatic: Hui appointed his younger brother Dun interior minister of Jingling, left ten thousand men under him for overall retention duties, and led twenty thousand men from Jiangling; he arrayed ships from the Jiang crossing to Pozhong—the banners blotted out the sun—and sighed, "I only regret that these cannot serve as an army to rescue the throne!"

sentences.zh: 晦欲遣兵襲湘州刺史張邵，何承天以邵兄益州刺史茂度與晦善，曰：「邵意趣未可知，不宜遽擊之。」

translations.literal: Hui wished to dispatch troops to strike Zhang Shao, governor of Xiang Province. He Chengtian, because Shao's elder brother Maodu, governor of Yi Province, was on good terms with Hui, said: "Shao's inclinations are not yet known—it is inadvisable to attack him hastily."
translations.idiomatic: Hui wished to dispatch troops to strike Zhang Shao, governor of Xiang Province. He Chengtian, because Shao's elder brother Maodu, governor of Yi Province, was on good terms with Hui, said, "Shao's inclinations are not yet known—it is inadvisable to attack him hastily."

sentences.zh: 晦以書招邵，邵不從。。

translations.literal: Hui tried to win Shao by letter; Shao would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Hui tried to win Shao by letter; Shao would not follow.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊午，以金紫光祿大夫王敬弘為尚書左僕射，建安太守鄭鮮之為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuwu, Wang Jinghong, Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Tassel, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Zheng Xianzhi, governor of Jian'an, was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuwu, Wang Jinghong, Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Tassel, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Zheng Xianzhi, governor of Jian'an, was made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 敬弘，廙之曾孫也。。

translations.literal: Jinghong was a great-grandson of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghong was a great-grandson of Yi.

sentences.zh: 庚申，上發建康。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the Emperor set out from Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the Emperor set out from Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 命王弘與彭城王義康居守，入居中書下省；

translations.literal: He ordered Wang Hong and Prince Pengcheng Yikang to remain and guard the capital, entering and dwelling in the lower offices of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wang Hong and Prince Pengcheng Yikang to remain and guard the capital, entering and dwelling in the lower offices of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 侍中殷景仁參掌留任；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yin Jingren shared in managing retention duties;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yin Jingren shared in managing retention duties;

sentences.zh: 帝姊會稽長公主留止台內，總攝六宮。。

translations.literal: the Emperor's elder sister, the Princess of Kuaiji, remained within the palace precinct and supervised the Six Palaces overall.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor's elder sister, the Princess of Kuaiji, remained within the palace precinct and supervised the Six Palaces overall.

sentences.zh: 謝晦自江陵東下，何承天留府不從。

translations.literal: Xie Hui went east from Jiangling; He Chengtian remained at headquarters and did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui went east from Jiangling; He Chengtian remained at headquarters and did not follow.

sentences.zh: 晦至江口，到彥之已至彭城洲。

translations.literal: When Hui reached the river mouth, Dao Yanzhi had already reached Pengcheng Isle.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui reached the river mouth, Dao Yanzhi had already reached Pengcheng Isle.

sentences.zh: 庾登之據巴陵，畏懦不敢進；

translations.literal: Yu Dengzhi held Baling but, fearful and timid, dared not advance;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dengzhi held Baling but, fearful and timid, dared not advance;

sentences.zh: 會霖雨連日，參軍劉和之曰：「彼此共有雨耳；

translations.literal: As heavy rain fell for days on end, Staff Officer Liu Hezhi said: "Both sides share the same rain;
translations.idiomatic: As heavy rain fell for days on end, Staff Officer Liu Hezhi said, "Both sides share the same rain;

sentences.zh: 檀征北尋至，東軍方強，唯宜速戰。」

translations.literal: the Northern Expedition General Tan will soon arrive—the eastern army is just growing strong; we should only fight quickly."
translations.idiomatic: General Tan the Northern Expedition will soon arrive—the eastern army is only growing stronger; we must fight at once."

sentences.zh: 登之恇怯，使小將陳祐作大囊，貯茅懸於帆檣，雲可以焚艦，用火宜須晴，以緩戰期。

translations.literal: Dengzhi, craven, had a junior officer Chen You make great sacks, fill them with thatch, and hang them from masts and sails, claiming they could burn ships; fire required clear weather—thus to delay the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi, craven, had a junior officer Chen You make great sacks, fill them with thatch, and hang them from masts and sails, claiming they could burn ships; fire required clear weather—thus to delay the battle.

sentences.zh: 晦然之，停軍十五日。

translations.literal: Hui agreed; he halted the army for fifteen days.
translations.idiomatic: Hui agreed; he halted the army for fifteen days.

sentences.zh: 乃使中兵參軍孔延秀攻將軍蕭欣於彭城洲，破之。

translations.literal: He then sent Central Army Staff Officer Kong Yanxiu to attack General Xiao Xin at Pengcheng Isle and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Central Army Staff Officer Kong Yanxiu to attack General Xiao Xin at Pengcheng Isle and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 又攻洲口柵，陷之。

translations.literal: He also attacked the stockade at the isle mouth and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked the stockade at the isle mouth and took it.

sentences.zh: 諸將鹹欲退還夏口，到彥之不可。

translations.literal: The generals all wished to retreat to Xiakou; Dao Yanzhi would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all wished to retreat to Xiakou; Dao Yanzhi would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 乃保隱圻。

translations.literal: They therefore held Yinfan.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore held Yinfan.

sentences.zh: 晦又上表自訟，且自矜其捷，曰：「陛下若梟四凶於廟庭，懸三監於降闕，臣便勒眾旋旗，還保所任。」。

translations.literal: Hui again submitted a memorial pleading his own case and also boasting of his victory, saying: "If Your Majesty would execute the Four Evils in the ancestral temple courtyard and hang the Three Overseers at the surrendered gate, your servant will then rein in the host, turn the banners, and return to guard my post."
translations.idiomatic: Hui again submitted a memorial pleading his own case and also boasting of his victory, saying, "If Your Majesty would execute the Four Evils in the ancestral temple courtyard and hang the Three Overseers at the surrendered gate, your servant will then rein in the host, turn the banners, and return to guard my post."

sentences.zh: 初，晦與徐羨之、傅亮為自全之計，以為晦據上流，而檀道濟鎮廣陵，各有強兵，足以制朝廷；

translations.literal: Earlier, Hui together with Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang had made a plan for self-preservation: they thought that with Hui holding the upper Yangtze and Tan Daoji garrisoned at Guangling, each having strong troops, they would be enough to control the court;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hui together with Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang had made a plan for self-preservation: they thought that with Hui holding the upper Yangtze and Tan Daoji garrisoned at Guangling, each having strong troops, they would be enough to control the court;

sentences.zh: 羨之、亮居中秉權，可得持久。

translations.literal: with Xianzhi and Liang holding power at the center, they could endure long.
translations.idiomatic: with Xianzhi and Liang holding power at the center, they could endure long.

sentences.zh: 及聞道濟帥眾來上，惶懼無計。。

translations.literal: When they heard that Daoji was leading troops upstream, they were fearful and without plan.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard that Daoji was leading troops upstream, they were fearful and without plan.

sentences.zh: 道濟既至，與到彥之軍合，牽艦緣岸。

translations.literal: Once Daoji arrived and joined Dao Yanzhi's army, they towed ships along the shore.
translations.idiomatic: Once Daoji arrived and joined Dao Yanzhi's army, they towed ships along the shore.

sentences.zh: 晦始見艦數不多，輕之，不即出戰。

translations.literal: Hui at first saw that the number of ships was not great and treated them lightly, not going out to fight immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Hui at first saw that the number of ships was not great and treated them lightly, not going out to fight immediately.

sentences.zh: 至晚，因風帆上，前後連咽；

translations.literal: By evening, as wind filled the sails they came upstream, bow to stern in unbroken succession;
translations.idiomatic: By evening, as wind filled the sails they came upstream, bow to stern in unbroken succession;

sentences.zh: 西人離沮，無復鬥心，戊辰，台軍至，忌置洲尾，列艦過江，晦軍一時皆潰。

translations.literal: the western men were scattered and dispirited, with no will to fight left. On wuchen the imperial army arrived at the tail of Jizhi Isle, deployed ships and crossed the river—the army of Hui all collapsed at once.
translations.idiomatic: the western men were scattered and dispirited, with no will to fight left. On wuchen the imperial army arrived at the tail of Jizhi Isle, deployed ships and crossed the river—the army of Hui all collapsed at once.

sentences.zh: 晦夜出，投巴陵，得小船還江陵。。

translations.literal: Hui went out by night, fled to Baling, obtained a small boat, and returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Hui went out by night, fled to Baling, obtained a small boat, and returned to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝遣雍州刺史劉粹自陸道帥步騎襲江陵，至沙橋；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor had ordered Liu Cui, governor of Yong Province, to lead infantry and cavalry by the land route to strike Jiangling, and he reached Shaqiao;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Emperor had ordered Liu Cui, governor of Yong Province, to lead infantry and cavalry by the land route to strike Jiangling, and he reached Shaqiao;

sentences.zh: 周超帥萬餘人逆戰，大破之，士眾傷死者過半。

translations.literal: Zhou Chao led more than ten thousand men to meet him in battle and routed him; more than half of the troops were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chao led more than ten thousand men to meet him in battle and routed him; more than half of the troops were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 俄而晦敗問至。

translations.literal: Before long, news of Hui's defeat arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, news of Hui's defeat arrived.

sentences.zh: 初，晦以粹善，以粹子曠之為參軍；

translations.literal: Earlier, Hui, regarding Cui as trustworthy, had made Cui's son Kuangzhi a staff officer;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hui, regarding Cui as trustworthy, had made Cui's son Kuangzhi a staff officer;

sentences.zh: 帝疑之，王弘曰：「粹無私，必無憂也。」

translations.literal: the Emperor was suspicious; Wang Hong said: "Cui has no private interests—there is surely no cause for worry."
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor was suspicious; Wang Hong said, "Cui has no private interests—there is surely no cause for worry."

sentences.zh: 及受命南討，一無所顧，帝以此嘉之。

translations.literal: When he received orders for the southern campaign, he gave no thought to personal concerns; the Emperor praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: When he received orders for the southern campaign, he gave no thought to personal concerns; the Emperor praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 晦亦不殺曠之，遣還粹所。。

translations.literal: Hui also did not kill Kuangzhi but sent him back to Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Hui also did not kill Kuangzhi but sent him back to Cui.

sentences.zh: 丙子，帝自蕪湖東還。。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the Emperor returned east from Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, the Emperor returned east from Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 晦至江陵，無它處分，唯愧謝周超而已。

translations.literal: When Hui reached Jiangling, he made no other dispositions but only apologized to Zhou Chao in shame.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui reached Jiangling, he made no other dispositions but only apologized to Zhou Chao in shame.

sentences.zh: 其夜，超捨軍單舸詣到彥之降。

translations.literal: That night, Chao abandoned the army, took a single boat, and went to Dao Yanzhi to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That night, Chao abandoned the army, took a single boat, and went to Dao Yanzhi to surrender.

sentences.zh: 晦從散略盡，乃攜其弟遯等七騎北走。

translations.literal: Hui's followers scattered and were nearly gone; he then took his younger brother Dun and six other riders and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's followers scattered and were nearly gone; he then took his younger brother Dun and six other riders and fled north.

sentences.zh: 遯肥壯，不能乘馬，晦每待之，行不得速。

translations.literal: Dun was stout and could not ride a horse; Hui waited for him each time, and they could not travel fast.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was stout and could not ride a horse; Hui waited for him each time, and they could not travel fast.

sentences.zh: 己卯，至安陸延頭，為戍主光順之所執，檻送建康。。

translations.literal: On jimao, they reached Yantou in Anlu and were seized by the garrison commander Guang Shunzhi, who sent them in a cage cart to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, they reached Yantou in Anlu and were seized by the garrison commander Guang Shunzhi, who sent them in a cage cart to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 到彥之至馬頭，何承天自歸。

translations.literal: When Dao Yanzhi reached Matou, He Chengtian surrendered of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: When Dao Yanzhi reached Matou, He Chengtian came in and surrendered on his own.

sentences.zh: 彥之因監荊州府事，以周超為參軍；

translations.literal: Yanzhi thereupon supervised the affairs of the Jing Province headquarters and made Zhou Chao an aide-de-camp;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi then took charge of the Jing Province headquarters and appointed Zhou Chao as an aide-de-camp;

sentences.zh: 劉粹以沙橋之敗告，乃執之。

translations.literal: Liu Cui reported the defeat at Shaqiao, and so [Yanzhi] had [Zhou Chao] seized.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cui reported the defeat at Shaqiao, and Yanzhi had Zhou Chao arrested.

sentences.zh: 於是誅晦、㬭、遯及其兄弟之子，並同黨孔延秀、周超等。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hui, Can, and Dun were executed, along with their brothers' sons and fellow conspirators Kong Yanxiu, Zhou Chao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xie Hui, Xie Can, and Xie Dun were put to death, together with their brothers' sons and fellow conspirators Kong Yanxiu, Zhou Chao, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 晦女彭城王妃被發徒跣，與晦訣曰：「大丈夫當橫屍戰場，奈何狼藉都市！」

translations.literal: Hui's daughter, the Princess of Pengcheng, with hair loose and barefoot, took leave of Hui, saying: "A great man ought to lie dead across the battlefield—how can he be scattered in disarray through the city streets!"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui's daughter, the Princess of Pengcheng, hair loose and barefoot, bade Hui farewell, saying, "A great man ought to fall dead on the battlefield—why end up strewn in disarray through the streets of the capital!"

sentences.zh: 庾登之以無任，免官禁錮；

translations.literal: Yu Dengzhi, for dereliction of duty, was stripped of office and confined;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dengzhi was stripped of office and confined for dereliction of duty;

sentences.zh: 何承天及南蠻行參軍新興王玄謨等皆見原。

translations.literal: He Chengtian, the acting aide-de-camp for the southern barbarians Wang Xuamo of Xinxing, and others were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian, Wang Xuamo of Xinxing, acting aide-de-camp for the southern barbarians, and the others were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 晦之走也，左右皆棄之。

translations.literal: When Hui fled, those around him all abandoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui fled, everyone around him deserted him.

sentences.zh: 唯延陵蓋追隨不捨，帝以蓋為鎮軍功曹督護。。

translations.literal: Only Yanling Gai followed after him without leaving; the Emperor appointed Gai Staff Officer and Supervisor of the Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanling Gai stayed with him to the end; the Emperor made Gai staff officer and supervisor of the Pacification Army.

sentences.zh: 晦之起兵，引魏南蠻校尉王慧龍為授。

translations.literal: When Hui raised troops, he sought the aid of Wang Huilong, Wei commandant of the southern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui raised troops, he sought support from Wang Huilong, the Wei commandant of the southern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 慧龍帥眾一萬拔思陵戍，進圍項城。

translations.literal: Huilong led ten thousand men, captured the Silin garrison, and advanced to besiege Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong led ten thousand men, took the Silin garrison, and advanced to besiege Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 聞晦敗，乃退。。

translations.literal: When he heard that Hui had been defeated, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Hui had been defeated, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史張茂度受詔襲江陵；

translations.literal: Zhang Maodu, governor of Yi Province, received orders to attack Jiangling;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maodu, governor of Yi Province, received orders to strike Jiangling;

sentences.zh: 晦敗，茂度軍始至白帝。

translations.literal: When Hui was defeated, Maodu's army had only just reached Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Hui was defeated, Maodu's army had only just reached Baidi.

sentences.zh: 議者疑茂度有貳心，帝以茂度弟邵有誠節，赦不問，使還。。

translations.literal: Some suspected Maodu of divided loyalty; the Emperor, because Maodu's younger brother Shao had shown faithful integrity, pardoned him without inquiry and ordered him to return.
translations.idiomatic: Some suspected Maodu of divided loyalty, but the Emperor, because Maodu's younger brother Shao had shown loyal integrity, pardoned him without inquiry and ordered him to return.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛己，帝還建康，征謝靈運為秘書監，顏延之為中書侍郎，賞遇甚厚。。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinji, the Emperor returned to Jiankang, summoned Xie Lingyun as Director of the Secretariat and Yan Yanzhi as Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, and rewarded them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinji, the Emperor returned to Jiankang, summoned Xie Lingyun as Director of the Secretariat and Yan Yanzhi as Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, and treated them with great favor.

sentences.zh: 帝以慧琳道人善談論，因與議朝廷大事，遂參權要，賓客輻湊，門車常有數十兩，四方贈賂相系，方筵七八，座上恆滿。

translations.literal: Because the monk Huilin was skilled at debate, the Emperor discussed major affairs of state with him; Huilin thus came to share in power and influence. Guests converged like spokes to a hub; there were often several dozen carriages at his gate; bribes streamed in from every quarter; seven or eight square banquets were laid out, and the seats were always full.
translations.idiomatic: Because the monk Huilin was skilled at debate, the Emperor discussed major affairs of state with him, and Huilin came to share in power and influence. Guests converged on him; there were often dozens of carriages at his gate; gifts and bribes poured in from every quarter; seven or eight square banquets were laid out, and the seats were always full.

sentences.zh: 琳著高屐，披貂裘，置通呈、書佐。

translations.literal: Lin wore high clogs, draped himself in a sable fur robe, and installed an office clerk and secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Lin wore high clogs, draped himself in a sable fur robe, and kept an office clerk and secretary at hand.

sentences.zh: 會稽孔覬嘗詣之，遇賓客填咽，暄涼而已。

translations.literal: Kong Yi of Kuaiji once called on him and found guests jamming the hall; he was merely greeted with a word about the weather.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yi of Kuaiji once called on him and found the hall packed with guests; Lin greeted him only with a remark about the weather.

sentences.zh: 覬慨然曰：「遂有黑衣宰相，可謂冠屨失所矣！」。

translations.literal: Yi said with indignation: "Here is a monk in black serving as chancellor—it is truly a case of cap and clogs out of place!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said with indignation, "We now have a monk in black serving as chancellor—cap and clogs have truly lost their proper place!"

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，乙未，以檀道濟為征南大將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史，到彥之為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fifth month, on yiwei, Tan Daoji was made Great General on the Southern Campaign, given an open office with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies, and appointed governor of Jiang Province; Dao Yanzhi was made governor of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on yiwei, Tan Daoji was made Great General on the Southern Campaign, given an open office with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies, and appointed governor of Jiang Province; Dao Yanzhi was made governor of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣散騎常待袁渝等十六人分行諸州郡縣，觀察吏政，訪求民隱；

translations.literal: Sixteen men including Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Yu were dispatched separately to the provinces, prefectures, and counties to observe the conduct of officials and inquire into the people's hidden grievances;
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen men including Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Yu were sent out separately to the provinces, prefectures, and counties to observe official conduct and inquire into the people's hidden grievances;

sentences.zh: 又使郡縣各言損益。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties were also ordered each to report what should be reduced or increased.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures and counties were also ordered each to report what should be cut back or expanded.

sentences.zh: 丙午，上臨延賢堂聽訟，自是每歲三訊。。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Emperor personally heard cases at the Hall for Extending Worth, and thereafter held three such sessions each year.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the Emperor personally heard cases at the Hall for Extending Worth, and thereafter held three such sessions each year.

sentences.zh: 左僕射王敬弘，性恬淡，有重名；

translations.literal: Wang Jinghong, Vice Director of the Left, was by nature tranquil and disinterested and enjoyed a great reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinghong, Vice Director of the Left, was by nature tranquil and disinterested and enjoyed a great reputation;

sentences.zh: 關署文案，初不省讀。

translations.literal: He never looked through the documents of the offices under his charge.
translations.idiomatic: He never even looked through the documents of the offices under his charge.

sentences.zh: 嘗預聽訟，上問以疑獄，敬弘不對。

translations.literal: Once, when he was present at a hearing of cases, the Emperor questioned him about a doubtful criminal matter, and Jinghong did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he was present at a hearing of cases, the Emperor questioned him about a doubtful criminal matter, and Jinghong did not answer.

sentences.zh: 上變色，問左右：「何故不以訊牒副僕射？」

translations.literal: The Emperor changed color and asked those around him: "Why were the interrogation documents not copied for the Vice Director?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face darkened and he asked those around him, "Why were the interrogation documents not copied for the Vice Director?"

sentences.zh: 敬弘曰：「臣乃得訊牒讀之，正自不解。」

translations.literal: Jinghong said: "Even when I did receive the interrogation documents and read them, I simply could not understand them."
translations.idiomatic: Jinghong said, "Even when I did receive the interrogation documents and read them, I simply could not understand them."

sentences.zh: 上甚不悅，雖加禮敬，不復以時務及之。。

translations.literal: The Emperor was very displeased; though he continued to treat Jinghong with courtesy, he no longer consulted him on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was very displeased; though he continued to treat Jinghong with courtesy, he no longer consulted him on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 六月，以右衛將軍王華為中護軍，待中如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wang Hua, Right Guard General, was made Central Army Protector, retaining his post as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Wang Hua, Right Guard General, was made Central Army Protector while retaining his post as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 華以王弘輔政，王曇首為上所親任，與己相埒，自謂力用不盡，每歎息曰：「宰相頓有數人，天下何由得治！」

translations.literal: Hua, because Wang Hong assisted in governing and Wang Tanshou was personally entrusted by the Emperor on a level with himself, felt his strength and ability were not fully used; he often sighed and said: "There are suddenly several chancellors—how can the realm ever be well governed!"
translations.idiomatic: Hua saw that Wang Hong was helping govern the realm and that Wang Tanshou enjoyed the Emperor's personal trust on a level with himself; feeling his own strength and ability were not fully used, he often sighed and said, "There are suddenly several chancellors—how can the realm ever be well governed!"

sentences.zh: 是時，宰相無常官，唯人主所與議論政事、委以機密者，皆宰相也，故華有是言。

translations.literal: At this time the chancellorship had no fixed office; whoever was discussed with by the ruler on affairs of state and entrusted with secrets was a chancellor—hence Hua's remark.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chancellorship had no fixed office; whoever the ruler discussed affairs of state with and entrusted with secrets counted as a chancellor—hence Hua's remark.

sentences.zh: 亦有任侍中而不為宰相者；

translations.literal: There were also men who held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary yet were not chancellors;
translations.idiomatic: Some men held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary yet were not chancellors;

sentences.zh: 然尚書令、僕，中書監、令，侍中，侍郎，給事中，皆當時要官也。。

translations.literal: Yet the Director and Vice Director of the Secretariat, the Supervisor and Director of the Central Secretariat, Attendants-in-Ordinary, Vice Directors, and Supervising Secretaries were all important offices of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Director and Vice Director of the Secretariat, the Supervisor and Director of the Central Secretariat, Attendants-in-Ordinary, Vice Directors, and Supervising Secretaries were all important offices of the day.

sentences.zh: 華與劉湛、王曇首、殷景仁俱為侍中，風力局干，冠冕一時。

translations.literal: Hua, together with Liu Zhan, Wang Tanshou, and Yin Jingren, all served as Attendants-in-Ordinary; in force of character and administrative capacity they were the ornament of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Hua, together with Liu Zhan, Wang Tanshou, and Yin Jingren, all served as Attendants-in-Ordinary; in force of character and administrative capacity they were the ornament of the age.

sentences.zh: 上嘗與四人於合殿宴飲，甚悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor once feasted and drank with the four men in the Hall of Union and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once feasted and drank with the four men in the Hall of Union and was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 既罷出，上目遂良久，歎曰：「此四賢，一時之秀，同管喉脣，恐後世難繼也！」。

translations.literal: When they had withdrawn, the Emperor gazed after them for a long time and sighed: "These four worthies, the finest of their time, together control lips and throat—I fear later ages will find them hard to match!"
translations.idiomatic: When they had withdrawn, the Emperor gazed after them for a long time and sighed, "These four worthies, the finest of their time, together hold the reins of state—I fear later ages will find them hard to match!"

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎謝弘微與華等皆上所重，當時號曰五臣。

translations.literal: Xie Hongwei, Vice Director at the Yellow Gate, together with Hua and the others, were all men the Emperor valued; at the time they were called the Five Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hongwei, Vice Director at the Yellow Gate, together with Hua and the others, were all men the Emperor valued; at the time they were called the Five Ministers.

sentences.zh: 弘微，琰之從孫也。

translations.literal: Hongwei was a grandnephew of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei was a grandnephew of Xie Yan.

sentences.zh: 精神端審，時然後言，婢僕之前不妄語笑，由是尊卑大小，敬之若神。

translations.literal: His spirit was composed and his bearing careful; he spoke only when the occasion called for it, and before maids and servants he never spoke or laughed lightly—wherefore high and low, great and small, revered him as a god.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit was composed and his bearing careful; he spoke only when the occasion called for it, and before maids and servants he never spoke or laughed lightly—wherefore high and low, great and small, revered him as a god.

sentences.zh: 從叔混特重之，常曰：「微子異不傷物，同不害正，吾無間然。」。

translations.literal: His cousin Hun set great store by him and often said: "Hongwei is distinct without harming things, alike without injuring integrity—I find no fault in him."
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Xie Hun set great store by him and often said, "Hongwei is distinct without harming things, alike without injuring integrity—I find no fault in him."

sentences.zh: 上欲封王曇首、王華等，拊御床曰：「此坐非卿兄弟，無復今日。」

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to ennoble Wang Tanshou, Wang Hua, and the others; he struck the imperial couch and said: "This seat—were it not for you brothers, there would be no today."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to ennoble Wang Tanshou, Wang Hua, and the others; he struck the imperial couch and said, "This seat—were it not for you brothers, there would be no today."

sentences.zh: 因出封詔以示之。

translations.literal: He then produced the enfeoffment edict and showed it to them.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced the enfeoffment edict and showed it to them.

sentences.zh: 曇首固辭曰：「近日之事，賴陛下英明，罪人斯得。

translations.literal: Tanshou firmly declined, saying: "In recent affairs, we have relied on Your Majesty's clear wisdom, and the guilty have been brought to justice.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou firmly declined, saying, "In recent affairs, we have relied on Your Majesty's clear wisdom, and the guilty have been brought to justice.

sentences.zh: 臣等豈可因國之災以為身幸！」

translations.literal: How could we take the realm's disaster as our own good fortune!"
translations.idiomatic: How could we turn the realm's disaster into our own good fortune!"

sentences.zh: 上乃止。。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon stopped.

sentences.zh: 魏主詔問公卿：「今當用兵，赫連、蠕蠕，二國何先？」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler issued an edict asking the high ministers: "We are about to use the army—between Helian and Rouran, which state should be attacked first?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor issued an edict asking the high ministers, "We are about to use the army—between Helian and Rouran, which state should be attacked first?"

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩、長孫翰、奚斤皆曰：「赫連土著，未能為患。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Song, Zhangsun Han, and Xi Jin all said: "Helian is settled on the land and cannot yet become a threat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Song, Zhangsun Han, and Xi Jin all said, "Helian is settled on the land and cannot yet become a threat.

sentences.zh: 不如先伐蠕蠕，若追而及之，可以大獲；

translations.literal: It would be better first to campaign against Rouran; if we pursue and overtake them, we can gain a great prize;
translations.idiomatic: It would be better first to campaign against Rouran; if we pursue and overtake them, we can gain a great prize;

sentences.zh: 不及則獵於陰山，取其禽獸皮角以充軍實。」

translations.literal: if we do not overtake them, we can hunt on Yin Mountain and take its beasts, hides, and horns to fill out military stores."
translations.idiomatic: if we do not overtake them, we can hunt on Yin Mountain and take its beasts, hides, and horns to fill out military stores."

sentences.zh: 太常崔浩曰：「蠕蠕鳥集獸逃，舉大眾追之則不能及，輕兵追之又不足以制敵。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Cui Hao said: "Rouran are birds that gather and beasts that flee; if a great host pursues them it cannot overtake them, and if light troops pursue them they are not enough to control the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Cui Hao said, "Rouran are birds that gather and beasts that flee; if a great host pursues them it cannot overtake them, and if light troops pursue them they are not enough to control the enemy.

sentences.zh: 赫連氏土地不過千里，政刑殘虐，人神所棄，宜先伐之。」

translations.literal: The Helian clan's territory is no more than a thousand li; their government and punishments are cruel and savage, abandoned by men and gods alike—they should be attacked first."
translations.idiomatic: The Helian clan's territory is no more than a thousand li; their government and punishments are cruel and savage, abandoned by men and gods alike—they should be attacked first."

sentences.zh: 尚書劉絜、武京候安原請先伐燕。

translations.literal: Minister of the Secretariat Liu Jie and Marquis of Wujing Anyuan asked to campaign against Yan first.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Secretariat Liu Jie and Marquis of Wujing Anyuan asked to campaign against Yan first.

sentences.zh: 於是魏主自雲中西巡至五原，因畋於陰山，東至和兜山。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Wei ruler personally toured west from Yunzhong to Wuyuan, hunted on Yin Mountain, and went east as far as Mount Hedou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Wei emperor personally toured west from Yunzhong to Wuyuan, hunted on Yin Mountain, and went east as far as Mount Hedou.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，還平城。。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 詔殿中將軍吉恆聘於魏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Palace Army General Ji Heng to go on a mission of courtesy to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Palace Army General Ji Heng to go on a mission of courtesy to Wei.

sentences.zh: 燕太子永卒，立次子翼為太子。。

translations.literal: Yong, crown prince of Yan, died; the second son Yi was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, crown prince of Yan, died; the second son Yi was established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐伐河西，至廉川，遣太子暮末等步騎三萬攻西安，不克，又攻番禾。

translations.literal: Chiqian, King of Qin, campaigned against Hexi, reached Lianchuan, and sent the crown prince Mumo and others with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Xi'an; they did not take it, and then attacked Fanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Chiqian, King of Qin, campaigned against Hexi, reached Lianchuan, and sent the crown prince Mumo and others with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Xi'an; they did not take it, and then attacked Fanhe.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜發兵御之，用遣使說夏主，使乘虛襲枹罕。

translations.literal: Mengsun, King of Hexi, sent troops to resist him and also sent envoys to persuade the Xia ruler to seize the opportunity and strike Bohan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun, King of Hexi, sent troops to resist him and also sent envoys to persuade the Xia ruler to seize the opportunity and strike Bohan.

sentences.zh: 夏主遣征南大將軍呼盧古將騎二萬攻苑川，車騎大將軍韋伐將騎三萬攻南安。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler sent Great General on the Southern Campaign Hulugu with twenty thousand cavalry to attack Yuanchuan and Chariot-and-Horse General Wei Fa with thirty thousand cavalry to attack Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler sent Great General on the Southern Campaign Hulugu with twenty thousand cavalry to attack Yuanchuan and Chariot-and-Horse General Wei Fa with thirty thousand cavalry to attack Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 熾磐聞之，引歸。

translations.literal: When Chiqian heard of it, he withdrew and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Chiqian heard of it, he withdrew and returned.

sentences.zh: 九月，徙其境內老弱、畜產於澆河及莫河仍寒川，留左丞相曇達守枹罕。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he moved the old and weak within his borders and livestock to the Jiao River, the Mo River, and the Naihan River, leaving Left Chancellor Tanda to guard Bohan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he moved the old and weak within his borders and livestock to the Jiao River, the Mo River, and the Naihan River, leaving Left Chancellor Tanda to guard Bohan.

sentences.zh: 韋伐攻拔南安，獲秦秦州刺史翟爽、南安太守李亮。。

translations.literal: Wei Fa attacked and took Nan'an, capturing Qin Governor of Qinzhou Zhai Shuang and Nan'an Administrator Li Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fa attacked and took Nan'an, capturing Qin Governor of Qinzhou Zhai Shuang and Nan'an Administrator Li Liang.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾握逵等帥部眾二萬餘落叛秦，奔昂川，附於吐谷渾王慕瑰。。

translations.literal: Wokui and others of Tuyuhun led more than twenty thousand households of their tribes to rebel against Qin, fled to Angchuan, and attached themselves to Murong Mugui, King of Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Wokui and others of Tuyuhun led more than twenty thousand households of their tribes to rebel against Qin, fled to Angchuan, and attached themselves to Murong Mugui, King of Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 大旱，蝗。。

translations.literal: Great drought; locusts.
translations.idiomatic: There was a great drought and a plague of locusts.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫范泰上表曰：「婦人有三從之義，無自專之道。

translations.literal: Fan Tai, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, submitted a memorial saying: "A woman has the three obediences and no way of acting on her own.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tai, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, submitted a memorial saying, "A woman has the three obediences and no way of acting on her own.

sentences.zh: 謝晦婦女猶在尚方，唯陛下留意。」

translations.literal: The women of Xie Hui's household are still in the Directorate of Palace Manufactories—may Your Majesty take note."
translations.idiomatic: The women of Xie Hui's household are still in the Directorate of Palace Manufactories—may Your Majesty take note."

sentences.zh: 有詔原之。。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 魏主聞夏世祖殂，諸子相圖，國人不安，欲伐之。

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler heard that Xia Shizu had died and his sons were contending with one another so that the people of the state were unsettled, he wished to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor heard that Xia Shizu had died and his sons were contending with one another so that the people of the state were unsettled, he wished to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩等皆曰：「彼若城守，以逸待勞，大檀聞之，乘虛入寇，此危道也。」。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Song and the others all said: "If they hold their cities and wait at ease for our weary force, and Datan hears of it and seizes the opportunity to raid us, that is a perilous course."
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Song and the others all said, "If they hold their cities and wait at ease for our weary force, and Datan hears of it and seizes the opportunity to raid us, that is a perilous course."

sentences.zh: 崔浩曰：「往年以來，熒惑再守羽林、鉤己而行，其占秦亡。

translations.literal: Cui Hao said: "Since last year Mars has twice guarded Yulin and moved along Gouji; the omen reads that Qin will perish.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao said, "Since last year Mars has twice guarded Yulin and moved along Gouji; the omen reads that Qin will perish.

sentences.zh: 今年五星並出東方，利於西伐。

translations.literal: This year the five planets all appear in the east—favorable for a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: This year the five planets all appear in the east—favorable for a western campaign.

sentences.zh: 天人相應，不可失也。」

translations.literal: Heaven and man correspond—this opportunity must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and man correspond—this opportunity must not be lost."

sentences.zh: 嵩固爭之，帝大怒，責嵩在官貪污，命武士頓辱之。

translations.literal: Song stubbornly argued against it; the Emperor grew furious, rebuked Song for corruption in office, and ordered warriors to humiliate him publicly.
translations.idiomatic: Song stubbornly argued against it; the Emperor grew furious, rebuked Song for corruption in office, and ordered warriors to humiliate him publicly.

sentences.zh: 於是遣司空奚斤帥四萬五千人襲蒲阪，宋兵將軍周幾是由萬人襲陝城，以河東太守薛謹為鄉導。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Minister of Works Xi Jin leading forty-five thousand men to strike Puban, and Zhou Ji, General of the Song Army, leading ten thousand men to strike Shancheng, with Hedong Administrator Xue Jin as guide.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he dispatched Minister of Works Xi Jin leading forty-five thousand men to strike Puban, and Zhou Ji, General of the Song Army, leading ten thousand men to strike Shancheng, with Hedong Administrator Xue Jin as guide.

sentences.zh: 謹，辨之子也。。

translations.literal: Jin was a son of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was a son of Xue Bian.

sentences.zh: 魏主欲以中書博士平棘李順總前驅之兵，訪於崔浩，浩曰：「順誠有籌略，然臣與之婚姻，深知其為人果於去就，不可專委。」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler wished to put Li Shun of Pingji, Doctor of the Central Secretariat, in overall command of the vanguard army; he consulted Cui Hao, who said: "Shun truly has stratagems, but I am related to him by marriage and know well that in decisive action he is swift to advance or withdraw—he cannot be wholly entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor wished to put Li Shun of Pingji, Doctor of the Central Secretariat, in overall command of the vanguard army; he consulted Cui Hao, who said, "Shun truly has stratagems, but I am related to him by marriage and know well that in decisive action he is swift to advance or withdraw—he cannot be wholly entrusted."

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon stopped.

sentences.zh: 浩與順由是有隙。。

translations.literal: From this Hao and Shun bore a grudge against each other.
translations.idiomatic: From this Hao and Shun bore a grudge against each other.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁巳，魏主發平城。。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingsi, the Wei ruler set out from Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on dingsi day, the Wei emperor departed from Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 秦左丞相曇達與夏呼盧古戰於嵻㟍山，曇達兵敗。

translations.literal: Qin's Left Chancellor Tanda fought with Xia's Hulügu at Mount Changmang; Tanda's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's left chancellor Tanda fought Xia's Hulügu at Mount Changmang, and Tanda's army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 十一月，呼盧古、韋伐進攻枹罕。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Hulügu and Weifa advanced to attack Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Hulügu and Weifa advanced to attack Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐遷保定連。

translations.literal: King Chi Pan of Qin moved to Baodinglian.
translations.idiomatic: King Chi Pan of Qin relocated to Baodinglian.

sentences.zh: 呼盧古入南城，鎮京將軍趙壽生帥死士三百人力戰卻之。

translations.literal: Hulügu entered the South City; the garrison-general of the capital Zhao Shousheng led three hundred death-defying soldiers and fought fiercely to drive him back.
translations.idiomatic: Hulügu entered the South City, but Zhao Shousheng, garrison-general of the capital, led three hundred death-defying soldiers and fought fiercely to drive him back.

sentences.zh: 呼盧古、韋伐又攻沙州刺史出連虔於湟河，虔遣後將軍乞伏萬年擊敗之。

translations.literal: Hulügu and Weifa again attacked Shazhou Governor Chulian Qian at the Huang River; Qian sent Rear General Qifu Wannian to strike and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Hulügu and Weifa again attacked Shazhou governor Chulian Qian on the Huang River; Qian sent Rear General Qifu Wannian to strike and defeat them.

sentences.zh: 又攻西平，執安西將軍庫洛干，坑戰士五千餘人，掠民二萬餘戶而去。

translations.literal: They again attacked Xiping, seized the pacifying-general of the west Kuluo Gan, buried alive more than five thousand warriors, plundered more than twenty thousand households of the people, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They again attacked Xiping, seized Kuluo Gan, pacifying-general of the west, buried alive more than five thousand warriors, plundered more than twenty thousand civilian households, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 仇池氐楊興平求內附。

translations.literal: Yang Xingping of the Di of Chouchi sought to submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingping of the Chouchi Di sought to submit to the court.

sentences.zh: 梁、南秦二州刺史吉翰遣始平太守寵咨據武興。

translations.literal: Ji Han, governor of the two provinces of Liang and South Qin, sent Shiping Administrator Chong Zi to occupy Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Han, governor of Liang and South Qin, sent Shiping administrator Chong Zi to occupy Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊產遣其弟難當將兵拒咨，咨擊走之。。

translations.literal: Di King Yang Chan sent his younger brother Nandang to lead troops to resist Zi; Zi struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Di king Yang Chan sent his younger brother Nandang to lead troops against Zi; Zi struck and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 魏主行至君子津，會天暴寒，冰合，戊寅，師輕騎二萬濟河襲統萬。

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler reached Junzi Ford, the weather suddenly turned bitterly cold and the ice closed over; on wuyin his army crossed the river with twenty thousand light cavalry to raid Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor reached Junzi Ford, the weather suddenly turned bitterly cold and the river froze over; on wuyin day his army crossed with twenty thousand light cavalry to raid Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 壬午，冬至，夏主方燕群臣，魏師奄至，上下驚擾。

translations.literal: On renwu, the winter solstice, the Xia ruler was just feasting his ministers when Wei forces suddenly arrived; above and below were alarmed and thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day, the winter solstice, the Xia ruler was feasting his ministers when Wei forces suddenly arrived; court and camp alike were thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 魏主軍於黑水，去城三十餘里。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler encamped at Black Water, more than thirty li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor encamped at Black Water, more than thirty li from the city.

sentences.zh: 夏主出戰而敗，退走入城。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler went out to battle and was defeated, then retreated and fled into the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler sallied out to fight and was defeated, then fled back into the city.

sentences.zh: 門未及閉，內三郎豆代田帥眾乘勝入西宮，焚其西門；

translations.literal: Before the gate could be closed, Inner Gentleman of the Third Rank Dou Daitian led his men to exploit the victory, entered the West Palace, and burned its west gate;
translations.idiomatic: Before the gate could be closed, Inner Gentleman of the Third Rank Dou Daitian led his men in on the momentum of victory, entered the West Palace, and burned its west gate;

sentences.zh: 宮門閉，代田逾宮垣而出。

translations.literal: the palace gates closed, and Daitian climbed over the palace wall and got out.
translations.idiomatic: when the palace gates closed, Daitian climbed over the palace wall and escaped.

sentences.zh: 魏主拜代田勇武將軍。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler appointed Daitian Brave Warrior General.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor appointed Daitian Brave Warrior General.

sentences.zh: 魏軍夜宿城北，癸未，分兵四掠，殺獲數萬，得牛馬十餘萬。

translations.literal: The Wei army encamped north of the city by night; on guiwei they divided their forces into four columns to plunder, killing and capturing tens of thousands, and obtained more than one hundred thousand cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army encamped north of the city overnight; on guiwei day they divided into four columns to plunder, killing and capturing tens of thousands and seizing more than one hundred thousand cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 魏主謂諸將曰：「統萬未可得也，它年當與卿等取之。」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said to the generals: "Tongwan cannot yet be taken; another year I shall take it together with you."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said to his generals, "Tongwan cannot be taken yet; another year I shall take it with you."

sentences.zh: 乃徙其民萬餘家而還。。

translations.literal: Thereupon he relocated more than ten thousand of their households and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then relocated more than ten thousand of their households and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏弘農太守曹達聞周幾將至，不戰而走。

translations.literal: Cao Da, Xia's administrator of Hongnong, heard that Zhou Ji was about to arrive and fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Da, Xia's administrator of Hongnong, heard that Zhou Ji was approaching and fled without fighting.

sentences.zh: 魏師乘勝長驅，遂入三輔。

translations.literal: The Wei army exploited the victory and drove deep, then entered the Three Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army pressed the victory and drove deep, entering the Three Assistants.

sentences.zh: 會幾卒於軍中，蒲阪守將東平公乙斗聞奚斤將至，遣使詣統萬告急。

translations.literal: Ji happened to die in camp; Puban's defending general, Duke Yidou of Dongping, heard that Xi Jin was about to arrive and sent an envoy to Tongwan to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Ji happened to die in camp; Yidou, Duke of Dongping and Puban's defending general, heard that Xi Jin was approaching and sent an envoy to Tongwan to report the emergency.

sentences.zh: 使者至統萬，魏軍已圍其城；

translations.literal: When the envoy reached Tongwan, Wei forces had already besieged the city;
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy reached Tongwan, Wei forces had already besieged the city;

sentences.zh: 還，告乙斗曰：「統萬已敗矣。」

translations.literal: returning, he told Yidou: "Tongwan has already been defeated."
translations.idiomatic: on his return he told Yidou, "Tongwan has already fallen."

sentences.zh: 乙斗懼，棄城西奔長安，斤遂克蒲板。

translations.literal: Yidou was afraid, abandoned the city, and fled west to Chang'an; Jin thereupon captured Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yidou abandoned the city and fled west to Chang'an; Jin thereupon captured Puban.

sentences.zh: 夏主之弟助興先守長安，乙斗至，與助興棄長安，西奔安定。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler's younger brother Zhuxingxian was defending Chang'an; when Yidou arrived, he and Zhuxingxian abandoned Chang'an and fled west to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler's younger brother Zhuxingxian was defending Chang'an; when Yidou arrived, he and Zhuxingxian abandoned the city and fled west to Anding.

sentences.zh: 十二月，斤入長安，秦、雍氐羌皆詣斤降。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jin entered Chang'an; the Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong all came to Jin to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Jin entered Chang'an, and the Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong all came to Jin to surrender.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜及氐王楊玄聞之，皆遣使附魏。。

translations.literal: Helan Mengsun, King of Hexi, and Di King Yang Xuan, hearing of this, both sent envoys to attach themselves to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Helan Mengsun, king of Hexi, and Di king Yang Xuan, hearing of this, both sent envoys to submit to Wei.

sentences.zh: 前吳郡太守徐佩之聚黨百餘人，謀以明年正會於殿中作亂，事覺，壬戌，收斬之。。

translations.literal: Former Wu Commandery Administrator Xu Peizhi gathered a faction of more than a hundred men and plotted to raise a revolt in the palace at next year's New Year assembly; the affair was discovered, and on renxu he was arrested and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Former Wu commandery administrator Xu Peizhi gathered a faction of more than a hundred men and plotted to raise a revolt in the palace at the next New Year assembly; the plot was discovered, and on renxu day he was arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 營陽太妃張氏卒。。

translations.literal: Grand Consort Zhang of Yingyang died.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Consort Zhang of Yingyang died.

sentences.zh: 秦征南將軍吉毘鎮南漒，隴西人辛澹帥戶三千據城逐毘，毘走還枹罕，澹南奔億池。。

translations.literal: Qin's southern-campaigning general Ji Pi garrisoned Nanchang; Xin Dan of Longxi led three thousand households to seize the city and drive Pi out; Pi fled back to Fuhan, and Dan fled south to Yichi.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's southern-campaigning general Ji Pi garrisoned Nanchang; Xin Dan of Longxi led three thousand households to seize the city and drive Pi out; Pi fled back to Fuhan, and Dan fled south to Yichi.

sentences.zh: 魏初得中原，民多逃隱。

translations.literal: When Wei first gained the Central Plains, many of the people hid and evaded registration.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei first gained the Central Plains, many people hid from registration.

sentences.zh: 天興中，詔采諸漏戶，令輸繒帛；

translations.literal: In the Tianxing era an edict collected all unregistered households and required them to pay silk tribute;
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianxing era an edict collected unregistered households and required them to pay silk tribute;

sentences.zh: 於是自佔為紬繭羅觳戶者甚眾，不隸郡縣，賦役不均。

translations.literal: thereupon very many declared themselves households of gauze, cocoon silk, crepe, and patterned silk, were not subject to commanderies and counties, and taxes and corvée were uneven.
translations.idiomatic: thereupon very many declared themselves silk-weaver households of gauze, cocoon silk, crepe, and patterned silk, exempt from county jurisdiction, and taxation and corvée became uneven.

sentences.zh: 是歲，始詔一切罷之，以屬郡縣。。

translations.literal: This year an edict first abolished all of this entirely and assigned them to commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: This year an edict abolished the practice entirely and assigned such households to the counties.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之上元嘉四年（丁卯，公元四二七年） 。

translations.literal: Above, first part of the reign of Emperor Wen the Literary: Yuanjia year 4 (dingmao; 427 CE).
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 4, fourth year of the reign of Emperor Wen—above, part one (dingmao; 427 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，帝祀南郊。。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinsi, the Emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on xinsi day, the Emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: On yiyou the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 統萬徙民在道多死，能至平城者什才六七。。

translations.literal: Of the people relocated from Tongwan, many died on the road; of those who could reach Pingcheng, only six or seven out of ten did so.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the people relocated from Tongwan died on the road; only six or seven out of ten reached Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏主如幽州。

translations.literal: On jihai the Wei ruler went to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day the Wei emperor went to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏主遣平原公定帥眾二萬向長安。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler sent Duke Ding of Pingyuan to lead twenty thousand men toward Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler sent Duke Ding of Pingyuan to lead twenty thousand men toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 魏主聞之，伐木陰山，大造攻具，再謀伐夏。。

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler heard of this, he felled trees on Yin Mountain, built siege equipment on a large scale, and again planned a campaign against Xia.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor heard of this, he felled trees on Yin Mountain, built siege equipment on a large scale, and again planned a campaign against Xia.

sentences.zh: 山羌叛秦。

translations.literal: The mountain Qiang rebelled against Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain Qiang rebelled against Qin.

sentences.zh: 二月，秦王熾磐遣左丞相曇達招慰武始諸羌，征南將軍吉毘招慰洮陽諸羌。

translations.literal: In the second month King Chi Pan of Qin sent Left Chancellor Tanda to summon and reassure the various Qiang of Wushi, and southern-campaigning general Ji Pi to summon and reassure the various Qiang of Yaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month King Chi Pan of Qin sent left chancellor Tanda to summon and reassure the Qiang of Wushi, and southern-campaigning general Ji Pi to summon and reassure the Qiang of Yaoyang.

sentences.zh: 羌人執曇達送夏；

translations.literal: The Qiang seized Tanda and sent him to Xia;
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang seized Tanda and sent him to Xia;

sentences.zh: 吉毘為羌所擊，奔還，士馬死傷者什八九。。

translations.literal: Ji Pi was struck by the Qiang, fled back, and of men and horses eight or nine out of ten were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Pi was routed by the Qiang and fled back; eight or nine out of ten of his men and horses were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 魏主還平城。。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，帝如丹徒，己巳，謁京陵。

translations.literal: On yimao the Emperor went to Dantu; on jisi he visited Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the Emperor went to Dantu; on jisi day he visited Jingling.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖既貴，命藏微時耕具以示子孫。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Gaozu had risen to eminence, he ordered his farming tools from humble days to be stored away to show his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Gaozu had risen to eminence, he had his farming tools from humble days stored away to show his descendants.

sentences.zh: 帝至故宮見之，有慚色。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached the old palace and saw them, he showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor reached the old palace and saw them, he looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 近侍或進曰：「大舜躬耕歷山，伯禹親事水土。

translations.literal: Some of those close at hand stepped forward and said: "Great Shun personally plowed on Mount Li, and Lord Yu personally attended to water and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Some of those close at hand stepped forward and said, "Great Shun personally plowed on Mount Li, and Lord Yu personally attended to water and earth.

sentences.zh: 陛下不睹遺物，安知先帝之至德，稼穡之艱難乎！」。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not behold these relics, how can you know the late Emperor's supreme virtue and the hardship of tilling and sowing!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not behold these relics, how can you know the late Emperor's supreme virtue and the hardship of tilling and sowing!"

sentences.zh: 三月，丙子，魏主遣高涼王禮鎮長安。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingzi, the Wei ruler sent Prince Li of Gaoliang to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingzi day, the Wei emperor sent Prince Li of Gaoliang to garrison Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 禮，斤之孫也。

translations.literal: Li was a grandson of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Li was a grandson of Jin.

sentences.zh: 又詔執金吾桓貸造橋於君子津。。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Commandant of the Capital Guard Huan Dai to build a bridge at Junzi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered Commandant of the Capital Guard Huan Dai to build a bridge at Junzi Ford.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，魏廣平王連卒。。

translations.literal: On dingchou Prince Lian of Guangping of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Prince Lian of Guangping in Wei died.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，帝還建康。。

translations.literal: On dinghai the Emperor returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day the Emperor returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 戊子，尚書右僕射鄭鮮之卒。

translations.literal: On wuzi Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Zheng Xianzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Zheng Xianzhi died.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐以輔國將軍段暉為涼州刺史，鎮樂都；

translations.literal: King Chi Pan of Qin appointed State-Supporting General Duan Hui as Governor of Liangzhou and garrisoned him at Ledu;
translations.idiomatic: King Chi Pan of Qin appointed state-supporting general Duan Hui governor of Liangzhou and garrisoned him at Ledu;

sentences.zh: 平西將軍麴景為沙州刺史，鎮四平；

translations.literal: he appointed Pacifying-General of the West Qu Jing as Governor of Shazhou and garrisoned him at Siping;
translations.idiomatic: he appointed pacifying-general of the west Qu Jing governor of Shazhou and garrisoned him at Siping;

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍出連輔政為梁州刺史，鎮赤水。。

translations.literal: and Northern-Pacifying General Chulian Fuzheng as Governor of Liangzhou and garrisoned him at Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: and northern-pacifying general Chulian Fuzheng governor of Liangzhou and garrisoned him at Chishui.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁未，魏員外散騎常侍步堆等來聘。。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingwei, Bu Dui, supernumerary attendant cavalier at large of Wei, and others came on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on dingwei day, Bu Dui, supernumerary attendant cavalier at large of Wei, and others came on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以廷尉王徽之為交州刺史，征前刺史杜弘文。

translations.literal: On gengxu Wang Huizhi, director of the Court of Judicial Review, was made Governor of Jiaozhou, and the former governor Du Hongwen was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day Wang Huizhi, director of the Court of Judicial Review, was made governor of Jiaozhou, and former governor Du Hongwen was summoned.

sentences.zh: 弘文有疾，自輿就路；

translations.literal: Hongwen was ill but set out on the road in a sedan chair;
translations.idiomatic: Hongwen was ill but set out on the road in a sedan chair;

sentences.zh: 或勸之待病癒，弘文曰：「吾杖節三世，常欲投軀帝庭，況被征乎！」

translations.literal: some urged him to wait until his illness healed; Hongwen said: "I have borne the imperial staff through three reigns and have always wished to give my body to the imperial court—how much more when I am summoned!"
translations.idiomatic: some urged him to wait until his illness healed; Hongwen said, "I have borne the imperial staff through three reigns and have always wished to give my body to the imperial court—how much more when I am summoned!"
