sentences.zh: 遂行，卒於廣州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set out and died at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He set out and died at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘文，慧度之子也。。

translations.literal: Hongwen was a son of Huinuo.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwen was a son of Huinuo.

sentences.zh: 魏奚斤與夏平原公定相持於長安。

translations.literal: Xi Jin of Wei and Duke Ding of Pingyuan of Xia faced off at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin of Wei and Duke Ding of Pingyuan of Xia faced off at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 魏主欲乘虛伐統萬，簡兵練士，部分諸將，命司徒長孫翰等將三萬騎為前驅，常山五素等將步兵三萬為後繼，南陽王伏真等將步兵三萬部送攻具，將軍賀多羅將精騎三千為前候。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler wished to exploit the opening to campaign against Tongwan; he selected troops and trained soldiers, assigned the generals, ordered Minister of Education Zhangsun Han and others to lead thirty thousand horsemen as vanguard, Wusu of Changshan and others to lead thirty thousand infantry as rear guard, Prince Fukang and others to lead thirty thousand infantry to escort siege equipment, and General He Duoluo to lead three thousand elite horsemen as advance scouts.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor wished to exploit the opening to campaign against Tongwan; he selected troops and trained soldiers, assigned the generals, ordered Minister of Education Zhangsun Han and others to lead thirty thousand horsemen as vanguard, Wusu of Changshan and others to lead thirty thousand infantry as rear guard, Prince Fukang and others to lead thirty thousand infantry escorting siege equipment, and General He Duoluo to lead three thousand elite horsemen as advance scouts.

sentences.zh: 素，遵之子也。

translations.literal: Su was a son of Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Su was a son of Zun.

sentences.zh: 五月，魏主發平城，命龍驤將軍代人陸俟督諸軍鎮大磧以備柔然。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Wei ruler set out from Pingcheng and ordered Dragon-Charger General Lu Hou of Dai to oversee the armies and garrison the Great Desert to guard against Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Wei emperor set out from Pingcheng and ordered Dragon-Charger General Lu Hou of Dai to oversee the armies and garrison the Great Desert against Rouran.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，濟君子津。。

translations.literal: On xinsi he crossed Junzi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day he crossed Junzi Ford.

sentences.zh: 壬午，中護軍王華卒。。

translations.literal: On renwu Central Palace Guard Wang Hua died.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Central Palace Guard Wang Hua died.

sentences.zh: 魏主至拔鄰山，築城，捨輜重，以輕騎三萬倍道先行。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler reached Balin Mountain, built a fort, left the baggage train behind, and with thirty thousand light cavalry went ahead at double speed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor reached Balin Mountain, built a fort, left the baggage train behind, and raced ahead with thirty thousand light cavalry at forced march.

sentences.zh: 群臣鹹諫曰：「統萬城堅，非朝夕可拔。

translations.literal: All the ministers remonstrated, saying: "The walls of Tongwan are strong and cannot be taken in a day or a night.
translations.idiomatic: All the ministers remonstrated, saying, "The walls of Tongwan are strong and cannot be taken quickly.

sentences.zh: 今輕車討之，進不可克，退無所資，不若與步兵、攻具一時俱往。」

translations.literal: Now to campaign against it with light forces—if we advance we cannot overcome it, and if we retreat we shall have no supplies; it would be better to go together with the infantry and siege equipment all at once."
translations.idiomatic: To campaign against it now with a light force—if we advance we cannot overcome it, and if we retreat we shall have no supplies—it would be better to go together with the infantry and siege equipment all at once."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「用兵之術，攻城最下。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "In the art of war, attacking walled cities is the worst option.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "In the art of war, storming walled cities is the worst option.

sentences.zh: 必不得已，然後用之。

translations.literal: One must have no alternative before using it.
translations.idiomatic: Only when there is no other choice should it be used.

sentences.zh: 今以步兵、攻具皆進，彼必懼而堅守。

translations.literal: Now if infantry and siege equipment both advance, they will surely be fearful and hold fast in defense.
translations.idiomatic: If we advance now with both infantry and siege engines, they will surely be alarmed and dig in.

sentences.zh: 若攻不時拔，食盡兵疲，外無所掠，進退無地。

translations.literal: If the attack does not succeed in timely capture, food exhausted and troops weary, with nothing to plunder outside, no ground to advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to take it quickly, our provisions will run out and our troops will be exhausted; with nothing to plunder outside, we will have nowhere to advance or retreat.

sentences.zh: 不如以輕騎直抵其城，彼見步兵未至，意必寬弛；

translations.literal: Better to use light cavalry to go straight to their city; when they see infantry has not yet arrived, their minds will surely be relaxed;
translations.idiomatic: Better to send light cavalry straight to their city; when they see the infantry has not yet arrived, they will surely let their guard down;

sentences.zh: 吾羸形以誘之，彼或出戰，則成擒矣。

translations.literal: I will show a weak form to lure them; if they perhaps come out to battle, then they can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: I will feign weakness to lure them out; if they venture out to fight, we can capture them.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，吾之軍士去家二千餘里，又隔大河，所謂『置之死地而後生』者也。

translations.literal: The reason for this is that my soldiers are more than two thousand li from home, and separated by a great river—the so-called "place them in death's ground and afterward they live."
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that my soldiers are more than two thousand li from home, cut off by a great river—they are in what is called "death's ground," where men fight to live.

sentences.zh: 故以之攻城則不足，決戰則有餘矣。」

translations.literal: Therefore using them to attack cities is insufficient, but for decisive battle there is surplus."
translations.idiomatic: Thus they are not enough for storming cities, but more than enough for a decisive battle."

sentences.zh: 遂行。。

translations.literal: With that he proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: With that he set out.

sentences.zh: 六月癸卯朔，日有食之。。

translations.literal: Sixth month, first day of guimao, the sun had an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month, guimao, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 魏主至統萬，分軍伏於深谷，以少眾至城下。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler arrived at Tongwan, divided the army and hid in a deep valley, with a small multitude came to the foot of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor reached Tongwan, divided his army and hid them in a deep valley, and with a small force rode up to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 夏將狄子玉降魏。

translations.literal: Xia general Di Ziyu surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia general Di Ziyu surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 言：「夏主聞有魏師，遣使召平原公定，定曰：『統萬堅峻，未易攻拔。

translations.literal: He said: "When the Xia ruler heard there was a Wei army, he sent an envoy to summon Duke of Pingyuan Ding. Ding said: 'Tongwan is strong and steep, not easily attacked and taken.
translations.idiomatic: He reported, "When the Xia ruler heard a Wei army was coming, he sent a messenger to summon the Duke of Pingyuan, Ding. Ding said, 'Tongwan is strong and steep and will not be easy to take.

sentences.zh: 待我擒奚斤，然後徐往。

translations.literal: Wait until I capture Xi Jin, then slowly go.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until I capture Xi Jin, then I shall come at my leisure.

sentences.zh: 內外擊之，蔑不濟矣。』

translations.literal: Attacking from inside and outside, nothing would fail to succeed.'
translations.idiomatic: Attacking from within and without, we cannot fail to succeed.'

sentences.zh: 故夏主堅守以待之。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Xia ruler held fast in defense and waited for him."
translations.idiomatic: So the Xia ruler dug in and waited."

sentences.zh: 魏主患之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor was troubled by this.

sentences.zh: 乃退軍以示弱，遣娥清及永昌王健帥騎五千西掠居民。。

translations.literal: Thereupon he withdrew the army to show weakness, and sent E Qing and Prince of Yongchang Jian leading five thousand cavalry west to plunder the inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew his army to feign weakness and sent E Qing and Prince Yongchang, Tuoba Jian, leading five thousand cavalry west to raid the countryside.

sentences.zh: 魏軍士有得罪亡奔夏者，言魏軍糧盡，士卒食菜，輜重在後，步兵未至，宜急擊之。

translations.literal: Among Wei army soldiers there was one who offended and fled to Xia, saying the Wei army's grain was exhausted, soldiers ate vegetables, baggage was in the rear, infantry had not arrived—it would be right to attack urgently.
translations.idiomatic: A Wei soldier who had committed an offense fled to Xia and reported that the Wei army had run out of grain, the soldiers were eating vegetables, the baggage train was still behind, and the infantry had not yet arrived—they should attack at once.

sentences.zh: 夏主從之。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler took his advice.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，將步騎三萬出城。

translations.literal: Jiachen, leading infantry and cavalry thirty thousand, he went out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, he led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry out of the city.

sentences.zh: 長孫翰等皆言：「夏兵步陳難陷，宜避其鋒。」

translations.literal: Changsun Han and others all said: "Xia troops' infantry formation is hard to breach; it is right to avoid their sharp edge."
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Han and others all said, "The Xia infantry formation is hard to break—better to avoid their charge."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「吾遠來求賊，惟恐不出。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said: "I came from afar seeking the enemy, fearing only that they would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said, "I came from afar seeking the enemy and feared only that they would not come out.

sentences.zh: 今既出矣。

translations.literal: Now they have already come out.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they have come out.

sentences.zh: 乃避而不擊，彼奮我弱，非計也。

translations.literal: Yet to avoid and not strike—them vigorous and us weak—is not a plan.
translations.idiomatic: To shrink from them now—making them bold while we look weak—is no strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 遂收眾偽遁，引而疲之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered the host and feigned flight, drawing them on to exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered his forces, feigned retreat, and drew them on to wear them down.

sentences.zh: 夏兵為兩翼，鼓噪追之，行五六里，會有風雨從東南來，揚沙晦冥。

translations.literal: Xia troops formed two wings, drumming and shouting in pursuit; after traveling five or six li, there happened to be wind and rain from the southeast, sand was raised and the sky was dark.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia troops split into two wings and pursued with drums and shouts; after five or six li, wind and rain blew in from the southeast, whipping up sand until the sky went dark.

sentences.zh: 宦者趙倪，頗曉方術，言於魏主曰：「今風雨從賊上來，我向之，彼背之，天不助人；

translations.literal: Eunuch Zhao Ni, who knew somewhat of occult arts, said to the Wei ruler: "Now wind and rain come from over the rebels; we face it, they have it at their backs—Heaven does not help men;
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhao Ni, who knew something of divination, told the Wei emperor, "The wind and rain are coming from the enemy's side; we face into it while they have it at their backs—Heaven is not helping us;

sentences.zh: 且將士飢渴，願陛下攝騎避之，更待後日。」

translations.literal: Moreover officers and soldiers are hungry and thirsty; I hope Your Majesty will gather the cavalry and avoid them, and wait for another day."
translations.idiomatic: Our officers and soldiers are hungry and thirsty; I beg Your Majesty to withdraw the cavalry and wait for another day."

sentences.zh: 崔浩叱之曰：「是何言也！

translations.literal: Cui Hao rebuked him, saying: "What words are these!
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao rebuked him: "What kind of talk is that!

sentences.zh: 吾千里制勝，一日之中，豈得變易！

translations.literal: We came a thousand li to win victory; within one day, how can we change!
translations.idiomatic: We marched a thousand li to win this battle—how can we change plans in a single day!

sentences.zh: 賊貪進不止，後軍已絕，宜隱軍分出，奄擊不意。

translations.literal: The rebels greedily advance without stopping; their rear army is already cut off—it is right to hide troops and divide them out, to strike unexpectedly.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is pressing forward without stopping and their rear is cut off—we should hide part of our army and strike them by surprise.

sentences.zh: 風道在人，豈有常也！」

translations.literal: The wind's path is in men—how can there be constancy!"
translations.idiomatic: Wind favors whoever seizes it—nothing is fixed!"

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said, "Excellent!"

sentences.zh: 乃分騎為左右隊以掎之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he divided cavalry into left and right companies to pin them.
translations.idiomatic: He then split his cavalry into left and right wings to pin the enemy.

sentences.zh: 魏主馬蹶而墜，幾為夏兵所獲；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler's horse stumbled and he fell, almost captured by Xia troops;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor's horse stumbled and threw him; he was nearly captured by Xia troops;

sentences.zh: 拓跋齊以身捍蔽，決死力戰，夏兵乃退。

translations.literal: Tuoba Qi used his body to shield and protect, fought with resolve to the death, and Xia troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Qi shielded him with his own body and fought with desperate fury until the Xia troops fell back.

sentences.zh: 魏主騰馬得上，刺夏尚書斛黎文，殺之，又殺騎兵十餘人，身中流矢，奮擊不輟，夏眾大潰。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler mounted his horse and got up, stabbed Xia Minister of Works Heli Wen and killed him, also killed more than ten cavalrymen; an arrow struck his body yet he fought on without ceasing, and the Xia multitude broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor remounted, ran through the Xia Minister of Works Heli Wen and killed him, then cut down more than ten horsemen; though an arrow struck him, he fought on without pause, and the Xia army broke in complete rout.

sentences.zh: 齊，翳槐子玄孫也。。

translations.literal: Qi was the great-great-grandson of Yihuai's son Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was the great-great-grandson of Xuan, son of Yihuai.

sentences.zh: 魏人乘勝逐夏主至城北，殺夏主之弟河南公滿及兄子蒙遜，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Wei men riding victory pursued the Xia ruler to the north of the city, killed the Xia ruler's younger brother Duke of Henan Man and elder brother's son Mengsun; dead were more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei pressed their victory and pursued the Xia ruler to the north of the city, killing his younger brother the Duke of Henan, Man, and his nephew Mengsun; more than ten thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 夏主不及入城，遂奔上邽。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler did not reach entering the city in time, and so fled to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler could not reach the city in time and fled to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 魏主微服逐奔者，入其城；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler in plain dress pursued those fleeing, entered their city;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor, dressed plainly, pursued the fugitives and entered the city;

sentences.zh: 拓跋齊固諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Tuoba Qi firmly remonstrated; he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Qi pleaded with him but was ignored.

sentences.zh: 夏人覺之，諸門悉閉；

translations.literal: Xia people discovered this; all gates were completely closed;
translations.idiomatic: The Xia realized what was happening and shut every gate;

sentences.zh: 魏主因與齊等入其宮中，得婦人裙，系之槊上，魏主乘之而上，僅乃得免。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler thereupon with Qi and others entered their palace, obtained a woman's skirt, tied it to a spear; the Wei ruler rode it up and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor went into the palace with Qi and the others, seized a woman's skirt, tied it to a spear, and climbed it to escape—barely making it out alive.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，夏尚書僕射問至奉夏主之母出走，長孫翰將八千騎追夏主至高平，不及而還。。

translations.literal: It happened to be dusk; Xia Vice Director of Masters of Writing Wen Zhi escorted the Xia ruler's mother in flight; Changsun Han led eight thousand cavalry pursuing the Xia ruler to Gaoping, did not catch up and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk, the Xia Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Wen Zhi, escorted the Xia ruler's mother in flight; Changsun Han led eight thousand cavalry in pursuit of the Xia ruler to Gaoping but failed to catch him and turned back.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，魏主入城，獲夏王、公、卿、將、校及諸母、后妃、姊妹、宮人以萬數，馬三十餘萬匹，牛羊數千萬頭，府庫珍寶、車旗、器物不可勝計，頒賜將士有差。。

translations.literal: Yisi, the Wei ruler entered the city, captured Xia kings, dukes, ministers, generals, officers, and all mothers, empresses and consorts, sisters, palace women numbering in the tens of thousands, horses more than three hundred thousand, cattle and sheep numbering in the tens of millions, storehouse treasures, chariots, banners, implements beyond counting; distributed rewards to officers and soldiers by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the Wei emperor entered the city and took captive Xia royalty, nobles, ministers, generals, officers, royal mothers, empresses and consorts, sisters, and palace women by the tens of thousands, along with more than three hundred thousand horses, tens of millions of cattle and sheep, and storehouse treasures, chariots, banners, and goods beyond reckoning; he distributed rewards to his officers and soldiers according to rank.

sentences.zh: 初，夏世祖性豪侈，築統萬城，高十仞，基厚三十步，上廣十步，宮牆高五仞，其堅可以厲刀斧。

translations.literal: Initially, Xia Shizu by nature was extravagant; he built Tongwan city ten ren high, foundations thirty paces thick, top ten paces wide; palace walls five ren high—their hardness could sharpen knives and axes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Xia emperor Shizu had been extravagant by nature; he built the city of Tongwan ten ren high, with foundations thirty paces thick and ten paces wide at the top; the palace walls stood five ren high, hard enough to sharpen knives and axes against them.

sentences.zh: 台榭壯大，皆雕鏤圖畫，被以綺繡，窮極文采。

translations.literal: Terraces and pavilions were grand and large, all carved and painted with pictures, covered with fine silks and brocades, exhausting all ornamental beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Its terraces and pavilions were vast, carved and painted throughout, draped in brocades and embroideries—a riot of ornament.

sentences.zh: 魏主顧謂左右曰：「蕞爾國而用民如此，欲不亡，得乎！」。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler turned and said to those at his side: "A puny state yet using the people thus—wishing not to perish, can it succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor turned to those around him and said, "A tiny realm, yet it drove its people like this—could it hope not to perish!"

sentences.zh: 得夏太史令張淵、徐辯，復以為太史令。

translations.literal: Obtained Xia Directors of Astronomy Zhang Yuan and Xu Bian, again made them Directors of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Xia Directors of Astronomy, Zhang Yuan and Xu Bian, and reappointed them to their old offices.

sentences.zh: 得故晉將毛修之、秦將軍庫洛干，歸庫洛干於秦，以毛修之善烹調，用為太官令。

translations.literal: Obtained former Jin general Mao Xiuzhi and Qin general Kuluo Gan; returned Kuluo Gan to Qin; because Mao Xiuzhi was skilled at cooking, used him as Chief Cook.
translations.idiomatic: He took the former Jin general Mao Xiuzhi and the Qin general Kuluo Gan; he sent Kuluo Gan back to Qin and, because Mao Xiuzhi was a gifted cook, made him Chief of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 魏主見夏著作郎天水趙逸所為文，譽夏主太過，怒曰：「此豎無道，何敢如是！

translations.literal: The Wei ruler saw writing by Xia Copying Director Zhao Yi of Tianshui; it praised the Xia ruler excessively; angry he said: "This petty fellow is without the Way—how dare he do thus!
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor read a text by the Xia Copying Director Zhao Yi of Tianshui that lavishly praised the Xia ruler and angrily said, "This scoundrel is utterly lawless—how dare he write like this!

sentences.zh: 誰所為邪？

translations.literal: Who wrote it?
translations.idiomatic: Who wrote this?

sentences.zh: 當速推之！」

translations.literal: He should quickly be traced!"
translations.idiomatic: Find out at once!"

sentences.zh: 崔浩曰：「文士褒貶，多過其實，蓋非得已，不足罪也。」

translations.literal: Cui Hao said: "Literary men in praise and blame often exceed reality; probably they had no choice—not enough to punish."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao said, "Men of letters in praise and blame often go beyond the truth; they likely had no choice—it is no crime worth punishing."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 魏主納夏世祖三女為貴人。。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler took three daughters of Xia Shizu as honored ladies.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor took three daughters of the Xia emperor Shizu as honored consorts.

sentences.zh: 奚斤與夏平原公定猶相拒於長安。

translations.literal: Xi Jin and Xia Duke of Pingyuan Ding still confronted each other at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin and the Xia Duke of Pingyuan, Ding, were still locked in stalemate at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 魏主命宗正娥清、太僕丘堆帥騎五千略地關右。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered Director of Imperial Clan E Qing and Grand Servant Qiu Dui to lead five thousand cavalry to raid territory in Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor ordered the Director of the Imperial Clan, E Qing, and the Grand Servant Qiu Dui to lead five thousand cavalry to raid the lands west of the pass.

sentences.zh: 定聞統萬已破，遂奔上邽；

translations.literal: Ding heard Tongwan was already broken, and so fled to Shanggui;
translations.idiomatic: When Ding heard that Tongwan had fallen, he fled to Shanggui;

sentences.zh: 斤追至雍，不及而還。

translations.literal: Jin pursued to Yong, did not catch up and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jin pursued as far as Yong but failed to catch him and turned back.

sentences.zh: 清、堆攻夏貳城，拔之。。

translations.literal: Qing and Dui attacked Xia Ercheng and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and Dui attacked the Xia city of Ercheng and captured it.

sentences.zh: 魏主詔斤等班師。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered Jin and others to return the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor ordered Jin and the others to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 斤上疏言：「赫連昌亡保上邽，鳩合餘燼，未有蟠據之資；

translations.literal: Jin submitted a memorial saying: "Hedie Chang fled to hold Shanggui, gathering remnant embers; he does not yet have resources to coil and hold fast;
translations.idiomatic: Jin memorialized, saying, "Hedie Chang has fled to Shanggui and is gathering what remains of his force; he does not yet have the strength to dig in and hold out;

sentences.zh: 今因其危，滅之為易。

translations.literal: Now while he is in peril, destroying him is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Strike him now while he is vulnerable and destroying him will be easy.

sentences.zh: 請益鎧馬，平昌而還。」

translations.literal: I request additional armor and horses, to pacify Chang and then return."
translations.idiomatic: I ask for more armor and horses so I can finish off Chang and then return."

sentences.zh: 魏主不許。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 斤固請，乃許之，給斤兵萬人，遣將軍劉拔送馬三千匹，並留娥清、丘堆使共擊夏。。

translations.literal: Jin firmly requested; thereupon it was granted; gave Jin ten thousand troops, sent General Liu Ba delivering three thousand horses, and kept E Qing and Qiu Dui to strike Xia together.
translations.idiomatic: Jin pressed his request until the emperor agreed, gave him ten thousand troops, sent General Liu Ba with three thousand horses, and kept E Qing and Qiu Dui to join him in attacking Xia.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，魏主自統萬東還，以常山王素為征南大將軍、假節，與執金吾桓貸、莫雲留鎮統萬。

translations.literal: Xinyou, the Wei ruler from Tongwan returned east; made Prince of Changshan Su General Who Subdues the South with acting staff, with Commandant of Excavated Gold Huan Dai and Mo Yun left to garrison Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, the Wei emperor set out east from Tongwan; he made Prince Changshan, Su, General Who Subdues the South with discretionary powers, and left him with the Commandant of the Guard, Huan Dai, and Mo Yun to garrison Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 雲，題之弟也。。

translations.literal: Yun was Ti's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Yun was the younger brother of Ti.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐還枹罕。。

translations.literal: King of Qin Juqen returned to Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin, Juqen, returned to Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己卯，魏主至柞嶺。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, jimao, the Wei ruler reached Zhaling.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jimao, the Wei emperor reached Zhaling.

sentences.zh: 柔然寇雲中，聞魏已克統萬，乃遁去。。

translations.literal: Rouran raided Yunzhong; hearing Wei had already captured Tongwan, thereupon fled away.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran raided Yunzhong, but when they heard Wei had taken Tongwan, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐謂群臣曰：「孤知赫連氏必無成，昌險歸魏，今果如孤言。」

translations.literal: King of Qin Juqen said to the ministers: "I knew the Hedie clan would surely not succeed; Chang rashly opposed Wei, and now indeed as I said."
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin, Juqen, told his ministers, "I knew the Hedie clan would never succeed; Chang rashly defied Wei, and now it has turned out exactly as I predicted."

sentences.zh: 八月，遣其叔父平遠將軍渥頭等入貢於魏。。

translations.literal: Eighth month, sent his uncle General Who Pacifies the Distance Wotou and others to offer tribute to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, he sent his uncle, the General Who Pacifies the Distance, Wotou, and others to present tribute to Wei.

sentences.zh: 壬子，魏主還至平城，以所獲頒賜留台百官有差。。

translations.literal: Renzi, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng, distributed what was captured to the resident capital officials by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng and distributed the spoils among the officials left at the capital according to rank.

sentences.zh: 魏主為人，壯健鷙勇，臨城對陣，親犯矢石，左右死傷相繼，神色自若；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler as a man was sturdy and strong, fierce and brave; facing cities and confronting battle lines he personally braved arrows and stones; those left and right died and were wounded in succession; his expression was calm;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor was sturdy, fierce, and bold; in siege and battle he personally braved arrows and stones, and though those around him fell wounded and dead in succession, his face never changed;

sentences.zh: 由是將士畏服，鹹盡死力。

translations.literal: Because of this officers and soldiers feared and submitted; all exerted death's effort.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this his officers and soldiers stood in awe of him and fought with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 性儉率，服御飲膳，取給而已。

translations.literal: By nature frugal and plain; dress, equipage, food and drink—taking supply only.
translations.idiomatic: He was frugal by nature; for dress, equipage, food, and drink he took only what he needed.

sentences.zh: 群臣請增峻京城及修宮室曰：「《易》云：『王公設險，以守其國。』

translations.literal: Ministers requested increasing height of the capital and repairing palace halls, saying: "The Changes says: 'Kings and dukes establish defenses to guard their states.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked to fortify the capital and build palace halls, saying, "The Book of Changes says, 'Kings and dukes establish defenses to guard their states.

sentences.zh: 又蕭何云：『天子以四海為家，不壯不麗，無以重威。』」

translations.literal: Moreover Xiao He said: 'The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as home; if not grand and not splendid, there is no way to magnify authority.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He also said, 'The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home; if the palace is neither grand nor splendid, it cannot inspire awe.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「古人有言：『在德不在險。』

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The ancients had words: 'In virtue, not in defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The ancients said, 'Security lies in virtue, not in walls.

sentences.zh: 屈丐蒸土築城而朕滅之。

translations.literal: Helian Bobo steamed earth to build walls and I destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo built walls of steamed earth, and I destroyed him anyway.

sentences.zh: 豈在城也？

translations.literal: How could it lie in walls?
translations.idiomatic: What do walls matter?

sentences.zh: 今天下未平，方須民力，土功之事，朕所未為。

translations.literal: Now all under Heaven is not yet at peace and the people's strength is still needed; works of earth and construction are what I have not undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is not yet at peace and still needs the people's strength; grand construction projects are what I have not undertaken.

sentences.zh: 蕭何之對，非雅言也。」

translations.literal: Xiao He's reply was not elegant speech."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He's reply was not elegant speech."

sentences.zh: 每以為財者軍國之本，不可輕費。

translations.literal: He always held that wealth is the foundation of army and state and must not be lightly spent.
translations.idiomatic: He always held that wealth is the foundation of army and state and must not be spent lightly.

sentences.zh: 至於賞賜，皆死事勳績之家，親戚貴寵未嘗橫有所及。

translations.literal: As for rewards and gifts, they went only to families with merit in death for the cause; kin and favorites were never given anything without cause.
translations.idiomatic: As for rewards and gifts, they went only to families with merit earned in death for the cause; kin and favorites never received anything without cause.

sentences.zh: 命將出師，指授節度，違之者多致負敗。

translations.literal: When he ordered generals to take the field he personally set out plans and dispositions; those who disobeyed often met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When he ordered generals to take the field he personally set out plans and dispositions; those who disobeyed often met defeat.

sentences.zh: 明於知人，或拔干於卒伍之中，唯其才用所長，不論本末。

translations.literal: He was clear in knowing men and sometimes raised the capable from the ranks, valuing only what their talents could do, without regard to origin.
translations.idiomatic: He was clear in knowing men and sometimes raised the capable from the ranks, valuing only what their talents could do, without regard to origin.

sentences.zh: 聽察精敏，下無遁情，賞不遺賤，罰不避貴，雖所甚愛之人，終無寬假。

translations.literal: His hearing and scrutiny were keen and sharp; below him nothing could be hidden. Rewards did not overlook the lowly, punishments did not avoid the noble—even those he loved most were never spared in the end.
translations.idiomatic: His hearing and scrutiny were keen; below him nothing could be hidden. Rewards did not overlook the lowly, punishments did not avoid the noble—even those he loved most were never spared in the end.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「法者，朕與天下共之，何敢輕也。」

translations.literal: He often said: "The law is what I share with all under Heaven—how dare I treat it lightly."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "The law is what I share with all under Heaven—how dare I treat it lightly."

sentences.zh: 然性殘忍，果於殺戮，往往已殺而復悔之。。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was cruel and decisive in killing; often he had already killed and then repented.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was cruel and decisive in killing; often he had already killed and then repented.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁酉，安定民舉城降魏。。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingyou, the people of Anding surrendered the whole city to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingyou day, the people of Anding surrendered the whole city to Wei.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊玄遣將軍苻白作圍秦梁州刺史出連輔政於赤炎。

translations.literal: Yang Xuan, king of the Di, sent the general Fu Baizuo to besiege Chulian Fuzheng, Qin's governor of Liangzhou, at Chiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan, king of the Di, sent the general Fu Baizuo to besiege Chulian Fuzheng, Qin's governor of Liangzhou, at Chiyan.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，民執輔政以降。

translations.literal: When grain in the city was exhausted, the people seized Fuzheng and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When grain in the city was exhausted, the people seized Fuzheng and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 輔政至駱谷，逃還。

translations.literal: Fuzheng reached Luogu Valley and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzheng reached Luogu Valley and fled back.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，秦以驍騎將軍吳漢為平南將軍、梁州刺史，鎮南漒。。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Qin made Wu Han, valiant cavalry general, Southern-pacifying General and governor of Liangzhou, stationed at Nanqiang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Qin made Wu Han, valiant cavalry general, Southern-pacifying General and governor of Liangzhou, stationed at Nanqiang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏主遣司馬公孫軌兼大鴻臚，持節策拜楊玄為都督荊、梁等四州諸軍事、梁州刺史、南秦王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Wei ruler sent the marshal Gongsun Gui, also grand master of splendid happiness, bearing credentials to invest Yang Xuan as commander of all military affairs in Jing, Liang, and four other provinces, governor of Liangzhou, and King of Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Wei emperor sent the marshal Gongsun Gui, also grand master of splendid happiness, bearing credentials to invest Yang Xuan as commander of all military affairs in Jing, Liang, and four other provinces, governor of Liangzhou, and King of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 及境，玄不出迎；

translations.literal: When he reached the border, Xuan did not come out to welcome him;
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the border, Xuan did not come out to welcome him;

sentences.zh: 軌責讓之，欲奉策以還，玄懼而郊迎。

translations.literal: Gui rebuked him and was about to return with the credentials; Xuan was afraid and went out to the suburbs to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui rebuked him and was about to return with the credentials; Xuan was afraid and went out to the suburbs to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 魏主善之，以軌為尚書。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler approved of this and made Gui director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor approved of this and made Gui director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 軌，表之子也。。

translations.literal: Gui was a son of Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was a son of Gongsun Biao.

sentences.zh: 十二月，秦梁州刺史吳漢為群羌所攻，帥戶二千還於枹罕。。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Wu Han, Qin's governor of Liangzhou, was attacked by various Qiang groups and led two thousand households back to Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wu Han, Qin's governor of Liangzhou, was attacked by various Qiang groups and led two thousand households back to Fuhan.
